 "document": {
  "id": "D10",
  "path": "early_draft_srs_galecia.txt",
  "text": "================================================================================
DRAFT SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION

FOR THE MANAGEMENT PROCESSES
OF AN
INTEGRATED LIBRARY SYSTEM

================================================================================

Prepared by:
Lori Ayre & Lucien Kress
Galecia Group
Consulting for Libraries and Cultural Heritage Organizations

Version: 1.0 DRAFT (for review)
Date: January 27, 2009
Status: Internal Draft - Circulating for Comment

================================================================================
TABLE OF CONTENTS
================================================================================

1. Executive Summary
2. Product Perspective
3. User Characteristics
4. Operating Environment Requirements
5. Design and Implementation Constraints
6. User Documentation Requirements
7. Assumptions and Dependencies
8. Functional Requirements - General Management Tools
9. Functional Requirements - Demographics
10. Functional Requirements - Inventory Control
11. Functional Requirements - Patron Records
12. Functional Requirements - Transaction Records
13. Functional Requirements - Financial Records
14. Appendices - Report Types
15. Fine-Grained Reporting Requirements

================================================================================
1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
================================================================================

This document presents a draft set of requirements for the management and
reporting processes of an Integrated Library System (ILS). These requirements
were developed for King County Library System (KCLS) in Washington State but
are believed to be applicable to many large, urban, multiple-branch,
centralized library systems.

The purpose of this document is to provide a comprehensive set of requirements
that can guide the development of reporting and management tools within an ILS.
The requirements cover functional aspects only; data structures and user
interfaces will require further specification and development using an
iterative, prototype-oriented methodology.

King County serves over 2.3 million residents across 49 libraries with an
annual circulation of approximately 8 million items. The system maintains
over 4 million bibliographic records and serves over 650,000 active borrower
accounts.

NOTE: This is a DRAFT document. Requirements are subject to change based on
feedback from stakeholders and additional analysis. Items marked [*] are
considered high priority by KCLS but may need adjustment for other systems.

================================================================================
2. PRODUCT PERSPECTIVE
================================================================================

The Management Processes component of an ILS provides the tools needed for
library administrators, managers, and staff to analyze operations, manage
collections, and make data-driven decisions. This component operates as part
of a larger enterprise-level Library Automation System.

The Management Processes are consolidated at a central location and accept
input from and provide services to multiple library locations. They rely on
the data structures and functionality of the broader ILS, including Acquisitions
and Cataloging modules.

The current specification presupposes the general functionality of an ILS and
specifies only those requirements that directly or indirectly relate to
management activities. While the requirements were developed specifically for
King County, they are expected to be suitable for many similar library systems.

The Management Processes facilitate the management of Library services,
programs, and policies. Specifically, the Management Processes support:

  - Analyzing the Library collection and its use by patrons.
  - Analyzing branch capacity and optimal distribution of the collection.
  - Analyzing the demographics and interests of patrons.
  - Analyzing staff productivity and workflow.
  - Tracking and verifying financial transactions.

================================================================================
3. USER CHARACTERISTICS
================================================================================

The following user types have been identified:

* Patron: A person utilizing the resources of a library, either as a member
  of the public with a library card or as a member of the public without a
  card. Patrons may interact with the system through the OPAC.

* Staff: Employees of the library system who are involved in designing and
  providing services to the public. This includes circulation staff, reference
  staff, and specialized staff.

* Local System Administrators: Individuals (typically library managers) who
  oversee library processes and have elevated permissions within the system.
  They can configure local settings and run system reports.

* Library Managers: Individuals who supervise organizational units and provide
  input to the design and implementation of library services. They use reports
  for planning and evaluation.

* Library Administrators: Senior leadership who plan and direct library services
  and priorities. They require aggregated, high-level reports for strategic
  planning and board presentations.

* Global System Administrator: The individual(s) who manage the ILS at the
  consortium level, implementing software changes and configurations, and
  generating statistical reports for the entire system.

================================================================================
4. OPERATING ENVIRONMENT REQUIREMENTS
================================================================================

OE-1: The system must support a library consortium with 286 locations, 17 million
      annual circulations, and purchasing/processing over 900,000 items per year.
      It is highly desirable that searches and reports can be processed during
      open hours without disrupting other system functions.
      [* High Priority]

OE-2: The system must operate on a Linux or Solaris server environment.
      [* High Priority]

OE-3: The system must be accessible through a web browser or a Windows-compatible
      client.
      [* High Priority]

OE-4: If web-browser based, the system must be accessible through Microsoft
      Internet Explorer (version 6.0 and later) and Mozilla Firefox (version
      2.0 and later).
      [* Medium Priority]

OE-5: The system must be accessible with screen-reading software, screen-
      magnification software, and other assistive technology programs designed
      to increase accessibility.
      [* High Priority]

================================================================================
5. DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINTS
================================================================================

CO-1: The system must use a fully relational database back-end. [* High Priority]

CO-2: The system must produce standards-compliant HTML output for web-based
      components.
      [* High Priority]

CO-3: The system must provide a development and training environment with the
      ability to migrate configurations to a production environment.
      [* Medium Priority]

CO-4: User rights and privileges will be controlled through security groups and
      or "roles" that allow access control for individuals, workgroups, and
      arbitrary staff groups.
      [* High Priority]

CO-5: These requirements must not constrain functionality or features of the
      Online Public Access Catalog (OPAC) module.
      [* High Priority]

================================================================================
6. USER DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS
================================================================================

UD-1: The developer must provide complete data specifications for authority
      records, bibliographic records, order records, item records, hold/request
      records, and other records maintained or accessed by the Management
      Processes.
      [* High Priority]

UD-2: The developer must provide a thorough high-level description of major
      processes, including bibliographic record import and export, validation
      of bibliographic records against internal and external authority sources,
      and standard reports.
      [* Medium Priority]

UD-3: The system must provide an online, hierarchical, and cross-linked help
      system in HTML that describes and illustrates all system functions.
      [* High Priority]

UD-4: The system must provide thorough high-level error reporting and feedback,
      and shall allow low-level query-specific feedback for Local and Global
      System Administrators from the front-end interface.
      [* Medium Priority]

================================================================================
7. ASSUMPTIONS AND DEPENDENCIES
================================================================================

AS-1: Management Processes are part of an enterprise-level Library Automation
      System.

DE-1: Management Processes rely on the data structures and functionality of an
      enterprise-level Library Automation System, including Acquisitions and
      Cataloging modules.

AS-2: Management Processes are consolidated at a central location, and accept
      input and provide services to multiple locations.

DE-2: Management Processes interface with a variety of vendor websites, via
      published APIs and/or automated transfer of standard-format data files
      (e.g., USMARC21, EDIFACT).

DE-3: Management Processes interact with a patron interface, also known as an
      Online Public Access Catalog (OPAC).

================================================================================
8. FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS - GENERAL MANAGEMENT TOOLS
================================================================================

[*] = High Priority item

8.1 Staff Login
The system should support streamlined methods of logging into terminals. For
example, a staff member could swipe a card (like an RFID employee badge) to
log in, or alternatively use individual login credentials (username and
password). The system should not REQUIRE card-based login - traditional
username/password should also be available as a fallback.

8.2 Report Templates
System administrators should be able to create report templates that are
available to staff. These templates should be runnable as-is or modifiable
for individual needs. Changes to templates should not compromise the accuracy
of results. Administrators should be able to limit which filters and display
fields can be altered, to certify a dependable output.

For example, front-line staff could set a call number range for a weeding
report or add/remove display fields from a pick list, but they should not be
able to alter the template to display deleted items.

8.3 Report Permissions
The system should provide distinct, fine-grained permission levels that limit
who can create and clone reports. All permissions should be easy to administer.
System administrators should be able to create shared folders to allow or
disallow staff from running specific reports, and/or to run ad hoc reports on
specific sets of data.

8.4 Query Tool
The system should provide a user-friendly interface for designing queries
against all record types (bibliographic, item, patron, transaction, financial).
Staff should be able to:
  - Select fields to query
  - Select values from a picklist of possible values
  - Select regular expressions from a drop-down menu
  - Use a full range of Boolean operators

Administrators should control staff access to tables and fields.

8.5 Board Reports / Executive Reports
The system should provide pre-defined reports for consumption by library boards
and other external consumers. These should include basic statistics like those
required by the Georgia Annual Report and Application for State Aid.

Activity reports should indicate traffic and volume of use, displaying
statistics on check-outs, check-ins, holds placed, and holds filled. It
should be possible to cross-tabulate per terminal, per branch, per library
system, per hour, per patron age range, per patron type, and per patron
location.

8.6 Transaction Data Archiving
Transactions should be archived in a form that protects patron privacy as
defined by State Law, while providing useful demographic statistics.

8.7 Periodic Report Examples
Examples of periodic reports include:
  - Bibliographic records with holds
  - Items that have not been checked out in X days
  - Item-level holds
  - Items with invalid item type
  - In-transit items with outstanding hold
  - Items that have been in-transit for more than X days
  - Items that are the last copy in the system
  - Items with a long call number
  - Missing items
  - Bibliographic records with no item records
  - Patrons with invalid home library

8.8 Query Selections Display
The system should provide the query selections along with the results, so users
can see what criteria were used to generate the report.

8.9 Report Queue
Staff should be able to see where their report is in the queue of reports
waiting to run.

8.10 Canned Report Examples
The system must be able to support the reporting definitions as described in
the attached report examples (see Appendix A).

8.11 Fine-Grained Reporting Requirements
The system must be able to support the fine-grained reports requirements as
described in the attached specification (see Appendix B).

================================================================================
9. FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS - DEMOGRAPHICS
================================================================================

9.1 Patron Behavior and Use Analysis
The system should produce statistics that can be used to understand and predict
patron behavior and use of materials. For example:
  - How quickly is a particular book returned, on average?
  - How likely is a particular book to be renewed?
  - What percent of check-outs at a particular branch are renewals?

9.2 Demographic Statistics
The system should produce useful demographic statistics, including transactions
by geographical regions, age ranges, etc. The data used to produce these
statistics must be anonymized - information that could be used to identify a
patron is deleted.

================================================================================
10. FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS - INVENTORY CONTROL
================================================================================

10.1 Material Volume Report
Ability to report on the volume of material in a given library at any point in
time, based on new acquisitions, items on the shelf, and items out in
circulation. The report should allow breaking down volume in categories such
as: total items in library, number of holds, number of adult fiction, number
of board books, etc.

10.2 System Capacity Interface
The system should provide an interface showing the capacity of all branches.

10.3 Shelf Space Report
For each genre and format of material, ability to compare:
  - The percentage of total circulations
  - The percentage of the collection
  - The percentage of total shelf space

The report should be able to run per library and per system.

10.4 Uncataloged Material
Ability to control inventory of uncataloged material, such as paperback books
and children's board books. Support needed for:
  - Quick distribution
  - Minimal branch labor
  - Ability to identify how the material is being used

Ability to count transactions and include in circulation statistics and
reports.

10.5 Item Transfer Utility
System should provide a utility for transferring batches of items between
branches. Uses include: moving books into a mobile library, an outreach program
collection, or a "just-in-time" warehouse.

The utility should include:
  - Ability to query for candidate materials
  - Ability to save queries for repeated use
  - Ability to manually select titles from query results
  - Ability to change records of selected items to move to new location
  - Mechanisms for moving items: changing location field, generating pull lists
  - Ability to revert items to original location after a set period of time

10.6 Missing and Damaged Items Report
The system should provide reports of missing and damaged items per branch.

10.7 In-Transit Items Report
The system should generate a list of items that have been in-transit for more
than X days (X configurable), per branch and per system. The report should
merge the transit-to and transit-from into one report for ease of front-line
staff use.

10.8 Item Record Purging
The system should provide a utility and reports for identifying item records
to purge, based on customizable criteria such as:
  - An item has been in status "missing" for more than X months
  - An item has status "discard/weed"

The system should have a report to assist in the conversion of items from one
status to another. The system should provide a last copy report that singles
out a library system's last copies, to assist catalogers who need to edit
WorldCat entries. The system should provide a quick effective method of
deleting volume entries along with copy entries, as well as records with no
items attached.

10.9 Deletions Tracking
Ability to count and track record deletions (e.g., item records, patron records)
per location and per system.

================================================================================
11. FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS - PATRON RECORDS
================================================================================

11.1 Patron Characteristics
Queries and reports can be limited or grouped by various patron characteristics,
including:
  - age range
  - zip code
  - county of residence
  - home branch
  - patron type
  - preferred language

11.2 Inactive Patrons Report
The system should generate a list of patrons with no circulation or electronic
activity in the last X days (X configurable). The list should be configurable
to System, Home Library, County, etc.

================================================================================
12. FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS - TRANSACTION RECORDS
================================================================================

12.1 Transaction History Maintenance
Transaction history is maintained for X days (X is configurable). Monthly and
annual aggregate information is maintained indefinitely.

12.2 Backroom Statistics Examples
Transactions can be grouped by hour, terminal, branch, and system. Transactions
include check-ins, check-outs, fines collected, patron registrations, etc., and
can be queried by all transactions or by type of transaction.

12.3 Types of Check-In
The system counts all types of check-in individually and cumulatively:
  - book-drop
  - by terminal
  - by user or self-service

12.4 Types of Check-Out
The system counts all types of check-out individually and cumulatively:
  - staff check-out
  - self check-out
  - staff renewal
  - self checkout renewal
  - online renewal
  - OPAC renewal

12.5 Holds and Locations
The system counts all hold requests, including how the hold was placed:
  - at a staff desk
  - at a public computer inside the library
  - remotely

12.6 Transactions Report
The system can generate a report of transactions (holds placed, holds filled,
and check-outs) per patron, per library, per selected group of libraries,
per system, per county. The system displays the number of check-outs and
placed holds per patron. Holds are subtotaled by type, e.g., active, frozen,
and frozen-until holds.

================================================================================
13. FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS - FINANCIAL RECORDS
================================================================================

13.1 Value of Items Report
The system can generate a report of the value of items (based on data in item
record) in the entire collection or a portion. Example: staff can obtain value
of all items with status of longoverdue, or value of all DVDs in children's
collection, or value of entire collection.

13.2 Standard Accounting Practice and Auditing Requirements
All reports and data archiving must comply with standard accounting practice
and state, county, and municipal auditing requirements.

13.3 Financial Data (Patrons)
Fines, charges, waivers, and ecommerce transactions are attached to patron
and item records. System tracks fines waived and payments made per library.
Financial information can be updated easily. As an example, a staff user can
easily query patron accounts with balances greater than X dollars.

13.4 Financial Reports
The system provides financial reports including:
  - patron account balances by patron, home library, and system
  - fines and charges accrued per time period (e.g., last twelve months, YTD,
    last month) and per type of charge (overdue fines, damaged item charges,
    lost item charges, etc.)
  - fines waived per time period and per branch
  - payments made per time period and per payment method (e.g., staff desk,
    self-check station, OPAC)

13.5 Financial Audit Trail
The system maintains a ledger of patron payments, including which charges
payments are applied to, to facilitate reconciliation.

================================================================================
14. APPENDIX A - REPORT TYPES
================================================================================

This appendix lists the various report categories and example report types
that have been identified as necessary.

CIRCULATION REPORTS:
- Check in Count
- Checkout Count (includes checkouts only)
- Items overdue by X days (daily, shelf reading, patron contact info)
- Circulation Count by Circ Modifier, Cat1, and Cat2 (Adult, YA, Juv...)
- Renewals Count
- Non-Cat Count
- Circulation Count - total circ including checkouts, renewals, and noncats
- Total Circulation Count (Merging both Cat and Non-Cat circulation data)
- Circulation Count by Dewey
- Circulation Count by Circ Modifier
- Circulation Count by Shelving Location
- Circulation Count by MARC
- Circulation Count by Circ Location broken down by Patron County
- Circulation Count by Circ Location broken down by Patron Home Library
- Circulation Count by Age Demographic

ITEMS REPORTS:
- Items Added Count
- Items Deleted Count
- List of Items Added
- Items Edited Count
- Items Count
- List of Items by Fines Stopped Reason
- Items Currently Checked Out
- Items more than XX days overdue (Overdue Materials Report)
- Items marked longoverdue by system
- List of Items with a > Total Use Count
- List of Items with a < Total Use Count [Weeding Report]
- Last Copy Report (last copy owned by a library system that was deleted)
- List of Items by Creation Date Range
- List of Items with a status of Missing
- List of Items in Transit by both sending library and destination library
- Claims returned
- List of Long Overdue
- Weeding report (date of last circulation and number of circs)
- List of items with XXX in bib record
- Age of collection by call number or shelving location
- Price value of collection by call number or shelving location
- Items to be Converted (batch converting items from one status to another)

BIB RECORDS REPORTS:
- Bib Records Count
- Bib Records Edited Count
- Bib Records Added by user by library Count
- Bib Records with No Volumes attached
- Bib Records missing specific MARC fields

PATRONS REPORTS:
- Patron Count
- Patron Added Count by Month
- New Patron Count (patrons added the previous month by Demographic Category)
- Patron Count by Age Demographic
- Patron Count by County
- Patron Count by County, City, and Zip Code
- Patron Count by Home Library
- Patron Count by Profile Group
- Patron Count by survey answer
- List of patrons by survey answer
- Voter Survey Responses County by Week
- List of Patrons by Expiration Date
- Voter Reg Survey Responses Count by Week
- List of patrons who are BARRED
- List of Patrons with inactive status
- List of Staff Accounts with date of last password change and account expiration
- List of Patrons with specific wording in notes

HOLDS REPORTS:
- Holds Purchase Alert
- Items Sent for Holds
- Items Received for Holds
- IntraPINES Loans for all Systems
- IntraPINES Loans for all Facilities
- IntraPINES Loans by System
- IntraPINES Loans by Facility
- Unfilled Holds
- Annual # of holds placed
- Stale Holds (holds sitting on hold shelf waiting for pickup for too long)

IN HOUSE USE REPORTS:
- NonCat In House Use Count by Month
- Cataloged In House Use Count

TRANSITS REPORTS:
- Items In Transit to Destination Library
- Items In Transit by Sending Library

BILLS REPORTS:
- Bills currently Owed by Patrons
- Detailed Payments Received
- Detailed Forgive, Work, and Goods Payments Received
- Detailed Voids
- Aged Debt

================================================================================
15. FINE-GRAINED REPORTING REQUIREMENTS
================================================================================

This appendix contains detailed requirements for the reporting interface and
functionality.

15.1 Three Interfaces
Three interfaces are needed:
  a) Canned reports - generic reports set to run by the individual either ASAP
     or recurring
  b) Noncanned or On Demand Reports - preset but have the ability to edit
     selection criteria and display options
  c) Open Template Reporting - all attributes associated with circulation,
     items, patrons, bills, and bibs to select from for filtering and display

15.2 Canned Reports Details
Canned reports are generic reports set to run by the individual either ASAP or
recurring. There should be a certain set of templates that are pre-written and
delivered with the product. Will have the ability for it to run by yesterday's
data, last week's, last month's, or last year's. Canned reports can be checked
off from a list to run at the same time and will be viewed within one document.

15.3 On Demand Reports
On Demand Reports would be for pre-selected criteria but for things like
maintenance reports or collections development and would be set to run on demand.

15.4 Open Template Reporting
Open template would have all attributes associated with say circulation,
patrons, items, bills, and bibs to select from for filtering and the same
attributes for displaying.

15.5 Quick Access Interface
- Ability to hover over each title of canned report/template with pop-up box
  with description
- Check off any part of data you want
- Ability to select Run ASAP, Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Yearly
- Output would be in Excel, HTML, and CSV format
- Ability to enter email addresses for report to be sent to - would be great to
  have an address book of regularly used addresses
- Ability to edit recurring reports by adding or removing report selections
  as well as editing the email addresses
- Ability to determine the output results in a way such that a result could have
  one column for last month's circs, another for previous month's circ, a percent
  difference column, previous year's month column, a percent difference from
  last month to last year's month column
- The system provides a report to assist in the batch conversion of statuses
- Ability to edit canned report for display purposes such as adding shelving
  location as a display
- Ability to add more canned reports via permission level
- Ability to get a list of items deleted that was the last copy owned by the
  library system in order to update WorldCat
- Ability to prioritize certain types of reports so they will pop to the top of
  the queue over resource-consuming reports
- Ability to have a total use count on items as well as a use count broken down
  by usage date range such as an FY use count or monthly use count
- Ability to retrieve total circ including checkouts, renewals, and noncats
  with a breakdown displaying those circ types
- Ability to upload a text file such as barcodes or TCN to use for filtering
  on a report
- Ability to run reports for pre-overdue, overdue, and holds notices sent
- Pivot table output
- Tested and proven output
- Ability to cancel a report that has already been scheduled to run or is
  currently running
- All nulls and blank fields must be included in the results no matter what is
  being filtered or displayed
- Ability to have real time reporting
- Ability to have historical reporting - a reporting warehouse such that data
  can be acquired on a given date or date range
- Selection criteria is clearly defined
- Report results would include the date selection criteria at the top or bottom
  to quickly see date range selected along with the name of the report
- Ability to select the survey name and not have to enter the survey id for
  filtering
- Ability to run a report on deleted items that were the last copy in the facility
- Ability to pull MARC record fields so that they appear on a single row of data
- Ability to run a report on transactions that occurred on x date and time on x
  workstation or by x staff

interviews, surveys, and working group discussions.

candidates.name: Consortium Operating Scale

candidates.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority.

candidates.name: Server Operating Environment
candidates.description: The system must operate on a Linux or Solaris server environment.
candidates.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority.

candidates.name: Client Access Platforms

candidates.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority.

candidates.name: Supported Web Browsers
candidates.description: When browser-based, the system must be accessible through Microsoft Internet Explorer version 6.0 or later and Mozilla Firefox version 2.0 or later.
candidates.source_priority_note: D10 marks this Medium Priority.

candidates.name: Assistive Technology Access
candidates.description: The system must be accessible with screen-reading software, screen-magnification software, and other assistive technology intended to increase accessibility.
candidates.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority.

candidates.name: Relational Database Backend
candidates.description: The system must use a fully relational database back-end.
candidates.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority.

candidates.name: Standards-Compliant HTML
candidates.description: Web-based components must produce standards-compliant HTML output.
candidates.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority.

candidates.name: Development Training Environment
candidates.description: The system must provide development and training environments with the ability to migrate configurations to production.
candidates.source_priority_note: D10 marks this Medium Priority.

candidates.name: Role-Based Access Control
candidates.description: The system must control user rights and privileges through security groups or roles that support access control for individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups.
candidates.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority.

candidates.name: OPAC Functionality Independence
candidates.description: The Management Processes requirements must not constrain the functionality or features of the Online Public Access Catalog module.
candidates.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority.

candidates.name: Record Data Specifications
candidates.description: The product documentation must provide complete data specifications for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold or request, and other records maintained or accessed by the Management Processes.
candidates.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority.

candidates.name: Process Description Documentation
candidates.description: The product documentation must provide thorough high-level descriptions of major processes, including bibliographic record import and export, validation of bibliographic records against internal and external authority sources, and standard reports.
candidates.source_priority_note: D10 marks this Medium Priority.

candidates.name: Online Hierarchical Help
candidates.description: The system must provide online, hierarchical, cross-linked HTML help that describes and illustrates all system functions.
candidates.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority.

candidates.name: Error Feedback
candidates.description: The system must provide thorough high-level error reporting and feedback, and low-level query-specific feedback through the front-end interface for Local and Global System Administrators.
candidates.source_priority_note: D10 marks this Medium Priority.

candidates.name: Streamlined Staff Login
candidates.description: The system should support streamlined staff terminal login using either an employee card such as an RFID badge or individual username and password credentials, with username and password available as a fallback rather than requiring card-based login.

candidates.name: Report Template Management
candidates.description: System administrators should be able to create report templates available to staff; staff should be able to run templates as-is or modify permitted selections, while template changes preserve result accuracy and administrators control which filters and display fields may be altered.

candidates.name: Report Permission Administration
candidates.description: The system should provide distinct, fine-grained, easily administered permissions controlling who may create and clone reports, and should let system administrators create shared folders that allow or disallow staff from running particular reports or running ad hoc reports on specified data sets.

candidates.name: Multi-Record Query Builder
candidates.description: The system should provide a user-friendly query-design interface for bibliographic, item, patron, transaction, and financial records, allowing users to select query fields, choose values from picklists, select regular expressions from a drop-down menu, and use Boolean operators, while administrators control staff access to tables and fields.

candidates.name: Executive Report Suite
candidates.description: The system should provide predefined reports for library boards and other external consumers, including basic statistics required by the Georgia Annual Report and Application for State Aid.

candidates.name: Activity Cross-Tabulation
candidates.description: Activity reports should show traffic and usage volumes for check-outs, check-ins, holds placed, and holds filled, with cross-tabulation by terminal, branch, library system, hour, patron age range, patron type, and patron location.

candidates.name: Privacy-Preserving Archives
candidates.description: The system must archive transactions in a form that protects patron privacy as defined by State Law while retaining useful demographic statistics.

candidates.name: Periodic Management Reports
candidates.description: The system should provide periodic reports for bibliographic records with holds; items not checked out in a configurable number of days; item-level holds; invalid item types; in-transit items with outstanding holds; items in transit beyond a configurable number of days; last copies; long call numbers; missing items; bibliographic records without item records; and patrons with invalid home libraries.

candidates.name: Query Criteria Display
candidates.description: The system should display the query selections or criteria together with report results so users can see which criteria generated the report.

candidates.name: Report Queue Visibility
candidates.description: Staff should be able to see the position of their report in the queue of reports waiting to run.

candidates.name: Patron Behavior Statistics
candidates.description: The system should produce statistics for understanding and predicting patron behavior and material use, including average return speed for a particular book, likelihood of renewal, and the percentage of check-outs at a branch that are renewals.

candidates.name: Anonymized Demographic Statistics
candidates.description: The system should produce demographic statistics such as transactions by geographic region and age range using anonymized data from which information that could identify a patron has been deleted.

candidates.name: Material Volume Reporting
candidates.description: The system must report the volume of material in a library at any point in time based on new acquisitions, shelf items, and items in circulation, with breakdowns such as total items, holds, adult fiction, and board books.

candidates.name: Branch Capacity Interface
candidates.description: The system should provide an interface showing the capacity of all branches.

candidates.name: Shelf Space Comparison
candidates.description: The system must compare, for each material genre and format and per library or system, the percentage of total circulations, percentage of the collection, and percentage of total shelf space.

candidates.name: Uncataloged Material Control
candidates.description: The system must control inventory of uncataloged materials such as paperback books and children's board books, supporting quick distribution, minimal branch labor, identification of material use, and counting these transactions in circulation statistics and reports.

candidates.name: Batch Item Transfers
candidates.description: The system must provide a utility for transferring batches of items between branches, including querying and saving candidate-material queries, manually selecting titles from results, changing selected item records to a new location, moving items by changing location fields or generating pull lists, and reverting items to their original location after a set period.

candidates.name: Missing Damaged Reports
candidates.description: The system should provide missing-item and damaged-item reports by branch.

candidates.name: In-Transit Reporting
candidates.description: The system should generate a merged report of items in transit for more than a configurable number of days, organized per branch and per system and combining transit-to and transit-from information for front-line staff.

candidates.name: Item Purge Management
candidates.description: The system must provide utilities and reports to identify item records for purging using customizable criteria, including items missing longer than a configurable number of months and items with discard or weed status; it must also support status-conversion reports, last-copy reports, deletion of volume entries with copy entries, and handling records with no attached items.

candidates.name: Deletion Tracking
candidates.description: The system must count and track deleted records, including item and patron records, by location and by system.

candidates.name: Patron Characteristic Filtering
candidates.description: Queries and reports must be limitable or groupable by patron age range, zip code, county of residence, home branch, patron type, and preferred language.

candidates.name: Inactive Patron Reporting
candidates.description: The system should generate a configurable report of patrons with no circulation or electronic activity during the previous configurable number of days, filterable or organized by system, home library, county, and similar organizational scope.

candidates.name: Transaction History Retention
candidates.description: The system must retain detailed transaction history for a configurable number of days and retain monthly and annual aggregate information indefinitely.

candidates.name: Transaction Grouping
candidates.description: The system must group transactions by hour, terminal, branch, and system and support querying all transactions or transaction types, including check-ins, check-outs, fines collected, and patron registrations.

candidates.name: Check-In Type Counts
candidates.description: The system must count check-ins both individually and cumulatively by book drop, terminal, and user or self-service source.

candidates.name: Check-Out Type Counts
candidates.description: The system must count check-outs both individually and cumulatively by staff check-out, self check-out, staff renewal, self-checkout renewal, online renewal, and OPAC renewal.

candidates.name: Hold Placement Counts
candidates.description: The system must count all hold requests and record how each hold was placed, including at a staff desk, at a public computer inside the library, or remotely.

candidates.name: Transaction Summary Reports
candidates.description: The system must generate transaction reports for holds placed, holds filled, and check-outs per patron, library, selected group of libraries, system, or county; display check-outs and placed holds per patron; and subtotal holds by types such as active, frozen, and frozen-until.

candidates.name: Collection Value Reporting
candidates.description: The system must report item values, based on item-record data, for the entire collection or a portion of it, including items selected by status, format, collection, or other report criteria.

candidates.name: Accounting Audit Compliance
candidates.description: All reports and archived data must comply with standard accounting practice and state, county, and municipal auditing requirements.

candidates.name: Patron Financial Records
candidates.description: The system must attach fines, charges, waivers, and ecommerce transactions to patron and item records, track fines waived and payments made per library, support easy financial-information updates, and allow queries such as patron accounts with balances above a specified dollar threshold.

candidates.name: Financial Report Suite
candidates.description: The system must provide reports of patron account balances by patron, home library, and system; fines and charges by time period and charge type; fines waived by time period and branch; and payments by time period and payment method, including staff desk, self-check station, and OPAC.

candidates.name: Payment Audit Ledger
candidates.description: The system must maintain a ledger of patron payments identifying the charges to which payments were applied, to support reconciliation.

candidates.name: Circulation Report Catalogue
candidates.description: The system must support circulation reports for check-in count; checkout count; items overdue by a specified number of days with daily, shelf-reading, and patron-contact information; circulation by circulation modifier, category, Dewey classification, shelving location, MARC data, patron county, patron home library, and age demographic; renewals; non-cataloged circulation; total circulation including checkouts, renewals, and non-cataloged circulation; and merged cataloged and non-cataloged circulation.

candidates.name: Item Report Catalogue
candidates.description: The system must support item reports for items added, deleted, edited, counted, currently checked out, overdue beyond a specified number of days, marked long overdue, above or below a total-use threshold, created within a date range, missing, in transit by sending and destination libraries, claimed returned, long overdue, containing specified bibliographic text, and items to be converted; reports must also cover fines-stopped reasons, last copies deleted by a library system, weeding data with last-circulation date and circulation count, collection age by call number or shelving location, collection price value by call number or shelving location, and items with specified total use.

candidates.name: Bibliographic Report Catalogue
candidates.description: The system must support reports for bibliographic-record counts, edited-record counts, records added by user and library, records with no attached volumes, and records missing specified MARC fields.

candidates.name: Patron Report Catalogue
candidates.description: The system must support reports for patron counts; patrons added by month; new patrons by demographic category; patrons by age, county, home library, profile group, survey answer, expiration date, inactive status, note wording, and barred status; survey-answer patron lists; voter survey responses by county and week; voter-registration survey response counts by week; and staff accounts showing last password change and account expiration.

candidates.name: Hold Report Catalogue
candidates.description: The system must support reports for hold purchase alerts; items sent or received for holds; IntraPINES loans for all systems, facilities, systems, and facilities; unfilled holds; annual hold counts; and stale holds waiting on hold shelves beyond the permitted pickup period.

candidates.name: In-House Use Reports
candidates.description: The system must support reports for non-cataloged in-house use counts by month and cataloged in-house use counts.

candidates.name: Transit Report Catalogue
candidates.description: The system must support reports for items in transit to a destination library and items in transit by sending library.

candidates.name: Bills Report Catalogue
candidates.description: The system must support reports for bills currently owed by patrons, detailed payments received, detailed forgive/work/goods payments received, detailed voids, and aged debt.

candidates.name: Canned Report Interface
candidates.description: The system must provide a canned-report interface for generic reports that individuals can run immediately or on a recurring schedule.

candidates.name: On-Demand Report Interface
candidates.description: The system must provide an on-demand report interface for preset maintenance, collection-development, and similar reports whose selection criteria and display options can be edited before execution.

candidates.name: Open Template Reporting
candidates.description: The system must provide open-template reporting with circulation, item, patron, bill, and bibliographic attributes available for both filtering and display.

candidates.name: Scheduled Report Access
candidates.description: The quick-access reporting interface must allow users to view descriptions by hovering over canned report or template titles, select portions of data, and schedule reports ASAP, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly.

candidates.name: Report Export Formats
candidates.description: Reports must be exportable in Excel, HTML, and CSV formats.

candidates.name: Report Email Delivery
candidates.description: The system must allow users to enter email addresses for report delivery and should provide an address book for regularly used addresses.

candidates.name: Recurring Report Editing
candidates.description: Users must be able to edit recurring reports by adding or removing report selections and changing their email addresses.

candidates.name: Comparative Report Columns
candidates.description: The system must support report outputs with comparative columns such as last month's circulation, the previous month's circulation, percentage difference, the corresponding month of the previous year, and percentage difference between the prior month and prior year's month.

candidates.name: Canned Report Extension
candidates.description: Authorized users must be able to add more canned reports according to permission level and edit canned-report display fields, such as adding shelving location.

candidates.name: Report Queue Prioritization
candidates.description: The system must allow certain report types to be prioritized above resource-consuming reports in the execution queue.

candidates.name: Item Usage Reporting
candidates.description: The system must provide total item-use counts and usage counts broken down by date ranges such as fiscal year or month.

candidates.name: Detailed Circulation Totals
candidates.description: The system must retrieve total circulation including checkouts, renewals, and non-cataloged circulation and display a breakdown by circulation type.

candidates.name: File-Based Report Filtering
candidates.description: Users must be able to upload a text file containing values such as barcodes or TCNs and use those values to filter a report.

candidates.name: Notice Activity Reports
candidates.description: The system must support reports on pre-overdue notices, overdue notices, and holds notices sent.

candidates.name: Pivot Table Output
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide pivot-table output.

candidates.name: Report Output Validation
candidates.description: Report output must be tested and proven accurate for its intended reporting purpose.

candidates.name: Report Cancellation
candidates.description: Users must be able to cancel a report that is scheduled to run or is currently running.

candidates.name: Include Null Fields
candidates.description: Report results must include all null and blank fields regardless of the selected filtering or display criteria.

candidates.name: Real-Time Reporting
candidates.description: The system must support real-time reporting.

candidates.name: Historical Reporting Warehouse
candidates.description: The system must support historical reporting through a reporting warehouse that can provide data for a specified date or date range.

candidates.name: Explicit Selection Criteria
candidates.description: The reporting interface must clearly define the selection criteria used for a report.

candidates.name: Report Date Metadata
candidates.description: Report results must display the selected date criteria and report name at the top or bottom of the results.

candidates.name: Survey Name Filtering
candidates.description: Users must be able to select a survey by survey name rather than entering its survey ID when filtering reports.

candidates.name: Last-Copy Deletion Reports
candidates.description: The system must provide reports identifying deleted items that were the last copy owned by a library system or facility, supporting WorldCat updates.

candidates.name: Single-Row MARC Fields
candidates.description: The system must be able to extract MARC record fields so that they appear on a single row of report data.

candidates.name: Workstation Transaction Reports
candidates.description: The system must support reports for transactions occurring on a specified date and time, workstation, or staff member.

outputs.description: The system must support reports for hold purchase alerts; items sent or received for holds; IntraPINES loans for all systems, facilities, systems, and facilities; unfilled holds; annual hold counts; and stale holds waiting on hold shelves beyond the permitted pickup period.

outputs.name: In-House Use Reports
outputs.description: The system must support reports for non-cataloged in-house use counts by month and cataloged in-house use counts.

outputs.name: Transit Report Catalogue
outputs.description: The system must support reports for items in transit to a destination library and items in transit by sending library.

outputs.name: Bills Report Catalogue
outputs.description: The system must support reports for bills currently owed by patrons, detailed payments received, detailed forgive/work/goods payments received, detailed voids, and aged debt.

outputs.name: Canned Report Interface
outputs.description: The system must provide a canned-report interface for generic reports that individuals can run immediately or on a recurring schedule.

outputs.name: On-Demand Report Interface
outputs.description: The system must provide an on-demand report interface for preset maintenance, collection-development, and similar reports whose selection criteria and display options can be edited before execution.

outputs.name: Open Template Reporting
outputs.description: The system must provide open-template reporting with circulation, item, patron, bill, and bibliographic attributes available for both filtering and display.

outputs.name: Scheduled Report Access
outputs.description: The quick-access reporting interface must allow users to view descriptions by hovering over canned report or template titles, select portions of data, and schedule reports ASAP, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly.

outputs.name: Report Export Formats
outputs.description: Reports must be exportable in Excel, HTML, and CSV formats.

outputs.name: Report Email Delivery
outputs.description: The system must allow users to enter email addresses for report delivery and should provide an address book for regularly used addresses.

outputs.name: Recurring Report Editing
outputs.description: Users must be able to edit recurring reports by adding or removing report selections and changing their email addresses.

outputs.name: Comparative Report Columns
outputs.description: The system must support report outputs with comparative columns such as last month's circulation, the previous month's circulation, percentage difference, the corresponding month of the previous year, and percentage difference between the prior month and prior year's month.

outputs.name: Canned Report Extension
outputs.description: Authorized users must be able to add more canned reports according to permission level and edit canned-report display fields, such as adding shelving location.

outputs.name: Report Queue Prioritization
outputs.description: The system must allow certain report types to be prioritized above resource-consuming reports in the execution queue.

outputs.name: Item Usage Reporting
outputs.description: The system must provide total item-use counts and usage counts broken down by date ranges such as fiscal year or month.

outputs.name: Detailed Circulation Totals
outputs.description: The system must retrieve total circulation including checkouts, renewals, and non-cataloged circulation and display a breakdown by circulation type.

outputs.name: File-Based Report Filtering
outputs.description: Users must be able to upload a text file containing values such as barcodes or TCNs and use those values to filter a report.

outputs.name: Notice Activity Reports
outputs.description: The system must support reports on pre-overdue notices, overdue notices, and holds notices sent.

outputs.name: Pivot Table Output
outputs.description: The reporting system must provide pivot-table output.

outputs.name: Report Output Validation
outputs.description: Report output must be tested and proven accurate for its intended reporting purpose.

outputs.name: Report Cancellation
outputs.description: Users must be able to cancel a report that is scheduled to run or is currently running.

outputs.name: Include Null Fields
outputs.description: Report results must include all null and blank fields regardless of the selected filtering or display criteria.

outputs.name: Real-Time Reporting
outputs.description: The system must support real-time reporting.

outputs.name: Historical Reporting Warehouse
outputs.description: The system must support historical reporting through a reporting warehouse that can provide data for a specified date or date range.

outputs.name: Explicit Selection Criteria
outputs.description: The reporting interface must clearly define the selection criteria used for a report.

outputs.name: Report Date Metadata
outputs.description: Report results must display the selected date criteria and report name at the top or bottom of the results.

outputs.name: Survey Name Filtering
outputs.description: Users must be able to select a survey by survey name rather than entering its survey ID when filtering reports.

outputs.name: Last-Copy Deletion Reports
outputs.description: The system must provide reports identifying deleted items that were the last copy owned by a library system or facility, supporting WorldCat updates.

outputs.name: Single-Row MARC Fields
outputs.description: The system must be able to extract MARC record fields so that they appear on a single row of report data.

outputs.name: Workstation Transaction Reports
outputs.description: The system must support reports for transactions occurring on a specified date and time, workstation, or staff member.

messages.content:
You are the editor of a software requirements specification. The user message is JSON with the FULL text of every input document (id, path, text) and the numbered candidate requirements extracted from each document separately (ref C001..., source document id, name, description, source_priority_note).

You see the whole corpus at once. That full-corpus context is what lets you judge duplicates across documents, which documents really support a requirement, and whether two statements genuinely conflict; use the documents, not only the candidates, for those judgements.

Work through the candidates as a checklist. Every candidate ends up in exactly one place, none is dropped silently:
- in a requirement's candidate_refs: duplicates go into the same requirement, and details go into their capability's requirement;
- in a blacklist entry's candidate_refs.
candidate_refs account for every catalogue-derived candidate individually.

Requirements: Options, fields, filters, sort orders, display rules, thresholds and similar details of one capability belong inside that capability's description, never in a separate requirement. Several distinct capabilities are never one requirement, even when they come from the same document, thread or stakeholder; sharing a topic is not a reason to merge. Each requirement has a short descriptive name (3 to 8 words) and a one-paragraph description that keeps the concrete facts (numbers, fields, roles). source_doc_ids are the documents that state or clearly imply the requirement; check the documents, a document that only shares the topic is not a source. Only explicit asks or clearly implied needs count. An open question, a complaint without a request, an aside, or a remark about what people do is not a requirement, and you add no capability the source does not mention (for example no extra operators or options for a query tool). Skip small talk and project process (meeting schedules, who should be interviewed, testing and QA process, assumptions about the team). Documentation and training that a source states as requirements of the software or product (for example user documentation items in a draft specification) are requirements and are kept. Never write a pointer requirement: a requirement states the capability itself, never "the reports listed in the specification/appendix", "see section X" or "the examples identified in ...". When a source contains a catalogue or list of items (for example an appendix of report types), each item becomes its own requirement or is explicitly folded into a named requirement whose description covers it. The description states only what the system must do or be: no provenance (which document, who said it) and no priority prose. Source priority signals go in source_priority_note instead: when a source marks the item with an explicit priority marker (for example [*] or "High") or calls it critical, mandatory, legally required or non-negotiable, write a short note naming the document id (for example "D10 marks this High; D06 calls it critical"); otherwise null. A note describes only its own item: never attach a signal a source gives for a different capability.

Blacklist: only items that are nonsensical (not a capability, rule or quality of the software) or genuinely incompatible with a better-supported requirement; prefer folding or rewording. Give the discarded item in full (name, description, source_doc_ids, candidate_refs) and a reason naming which sources back each side.

Glossary: one term per domain concept, used consistently in all names and descriptions, each with a one-sentence definition.

Open questions: questions the sources themselves leave open (for example an undefined metric, a threshold nobody fixed, an unresolved disagreement between stakeholders), each with the document ids where it arises. Do not invent questions.

system_name: a short noun phrase naming the system the corpus describes.

Definition of a requirement: A requirement describes one capability, rule or quality the system must provide, at the level a tester would write one acceptance test for. It names what, for whom, and under what condition, and it is independent of how it is implemented. Two statements are the same requirement if a tester would write one test for both. A statement is too broad if its acceptance test would have to be several unrelated tests. A statement is too narrow if it only makes sense as a detail of another requirement, such as one filter option of a report.

Example of a statement that is too broad: "Staff can manage item transfers between branches, including selecting candidate items by circulation history and keeping an audit history of every completed transfer." This is exactly two requirements: (1) select transfer candidates by circulation history, (2) record an audit history of completed transfers.
Example of statements that are too narrow: "The inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch" and "The inactive patron report can be filtered by patron profile". These are one requirement: the inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch and patron profile.

From a technical standpoint, this is doable but requires careful design.

1. Query builder for candidate selection - we can reuse the report query
   tool for this.

2. Save/share queries - similar to report templates.

3. Batch update of location field - straightforward database update with
   transaction safety.

5. Auto-revert mechanism - a scheduled task that checks transferred items
   and reverts them based on time or status criteria.

6. Logging - track all transfers for audit purposes.
