requirements.name: Material Volume Reporting
requirements.description: The system must report material volume for a specified library at the current time or a selected historical point, separating new acquisitions, items on the shelf, items in circulation, and totals. Users must be able to break results down by categories such as total items, holds, adult fiction, and board books, customize categories, and report volume added in periods such as the last 30, 60, or 90 days.

requirements.name: Branch Capacity Interface
requirements.description: The system must provide authorized users, including branch managers, an overview of capacity across all branches, with the ability to drill into individual branches, sort and filter by region, library type, and current load, view growth or shrinkage trends, and export the information to CSV. The capacity measure itself remains to be defined.

requirements.name: Shelf Space Usage Report
requirements.description: The system must compare, for each material genre and format, the percentage of total circulations, the percentage of the collection, and the percentage of total shelf space. Results must be available per library and system-wide, support date-range comparisons, and provide a side-by-side library comparison view. When shelf-space measurements are unavailable, the system must estimate shelf space using available item dimensions or item count as a proxy.

requirements.name: Transfer Item Batches
requirements.description: The system must provide a utility for transferring batches of items between branches or other locations, including mobile libraries, outreach collections, warehouses, book sales, and event locations.

requirements.name: Query Transfer Candidates
requirements.description: The system must allow authorized staff to query for candidate materials for transfer or other administrative processing, using conditions such as material type, section, genre, or circulation history.

requirements.name: Save Reusable Queries
requirements.description: The system must allow users to save queries for repeated use, including recurring transfer and reporting tasks.

requirements.name: Share Transfer Queries
requirements.description: The system must allow authorized users to share saved transfer queries with other authorized users.

requirements.name: Select Transfer Results
requirements.description: The system must allow staff to manually select individual titles or items from query results, including selecting only part of a larger candidate set for subsequent administrative processing.

requirements.name: Update Item Locations
requirements.description: The system must allow authorized staff to change the location records of selected items to the transfer destination.

requirements.name: Generate Transfer Pull Lists
requirements.description: The system must generate printable pull lists identifying items selected for transfer so staff can retrieve them for movement.

requirements.name: Preview Pending Transfers
requirements.description: Before applying a transfer, the system must show a preview of the proposed changes, including the number of items and their source and destination locations, and require confirmation before making the changes.

requirements.name: Undo Completed Transfers
requirements.description: The system must allow an authorized user to undo an item transfer when an incorrect transfer has been completed.

requirements.name: Revert Transferred Items
requirements.description: The system must automatically or manually return transferred items to their original locations after a configured period or when configured criteria are met. Supported criteria include time-based conditions and item-status or destination events; the sources do not establish whether checkout at the destination should trigger reversion.

requirements.name: Transfer History Records
requirements.description: The system must retain transfer activity for audit and expose item transfer history so staff can review completed and reverted transfers and determine how often an item has moved.

requirements.name: Print Transit Labels
requirements.description: The system must generate printable transit labels containing barcodes for items being transferred.

requirements.name: Restrict Transfer Permissions
requirements.description: The system must restrict item transfers to authorized roles, including managers, administrators, or transfer coordinators, and prevent unauthorized staff from performing transfers.

requirements.name: Alert Transfer Problems
requirements.description: The system must notify responsible staff when an item transfer is delayed or encounters an issue.

requirements.name: Missing Damaged Items Report
requirements.description: The system must provide a report of missing and damaged items by branch. The report must include item condition notes and support date ranges for trend analysis.

requirements.name: Delayed Transit Items Report
requirements.description: The system must generate one report of items that have remained in transit longer than a configurable number of days, with views per branch and system-wide. The report must combine transit-to and transit-from items, identify items with no arrival date and an overdue departure date, and allow sorting by due date. Seven days is suggested as the default threshold.

requirements.name: Transit Location Reports
requirements.description: The system must report items in transit by sending library and destination library, and provide reports of items currently in transit between locations for delivery coordination.

requirements.name: Identify Purge Candidates
requirements.description: The system must identify item records eligible for purging using customizable, combinable criteria, including status (such as missing, discard/weed, or damaged), time spent in a status, and time since last circulation.
requirements.source_priority_note: D06 marks the last-copy report critical; this note does not apply to purge-candidate identification.

requirements.name: Review Purge Candidates
requirements.description: The system must provide read-only reports of item records identified as purge candidates so users can review them without changing or deleting records through the reports.

requirements.name: Batch Status Conversion
requirements.description: The system must support converting multiple items from one status to another in a batch, such as changing items from missing to discard/weed, and provide a report or workflow to assist with the conversion.

requirements.name: Last Copy Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide last-copy reports identifying items that are the only copy within a selected scope, including an individual library and the entire consortium. Reports must also identify deleted items that were the last copy in a library system or facility, supporting catalogers' WorldCat updates.
requirements.source_priority_note: D06 marks the last-copy report critical; D15 calls it critical.

requirements.name: Delete Volumes With Copies
requirements.description: The system must provide a method to delete volume entries together with their associated copy entries during collection cleanup.

requirements.name: Delete Itemless Records
requirements.description: The system must provide a method to delete records that have no items attached during collection cleanup.

requirements.name: Confirm Purge Deletions
requirements.description: The system must require a separate confirmation step before executing purge deletions, distinct from identifying and reviewing candidates.

requirements.name: Audit Record Deletions
requirements.description: The system must retain an audit record of successful deletions, including record type, record identifier, timestamp, user, and user location. This tracking must cover purge activity and other record deletions.

requirements.name: Track Denied Deletions
requirements.description: The system must track deletion attempts that are denied so administrators can identify attempted deletions of records that users should not delete.

requirements.name: Report Deletion Activity
requirements.description: The system must report deletion activity for a selected period, including totals and breakdowns by record type, location, system, and user, and identify users with the highest deletion counts.

requirements.name: Filter Patron Reports
requirements.description: The system must allow patron queries and reports to be limited by age range, ZIP code, county of residence, home branch, patron type, and preferred language. Users must be able to combine these filters with other conditions using AND and OR logic.

requirements.name: Group Patron Reports
requirements.description: The system must group patron queries and reports by age range, ZIP code, county of residence, home branch, patron type, and preferred language, and show aggregates such as circulation counts and patron counts for each group.

requirements.name: Configure Patron Age Ranges
requirements.description: The system must allow age ranges used for patron filtering and grouping to be configured for each report and calculated from patrons' birth dates. Configurations must support user-defined brackets such as 0–5, 6–10, and 11–15.

requirements.name: Include Null Report Values
requirements.description: Report results must include records with null or blank values rather than silently excluding them, including patrons with unpopulated optional demographic fields.

requirements.name: Inactive Patron Reports
requirements.description: The system must generate lists of patrons with no circulation or electronic activity during a configurable number of days. Electronic activity includes account or OPAC logins, online holds, online renewals, and logged access to integrated digital collections. Users must be able to select System, Home Library, County, or another required organizational level; include current mailing addresses; separately identify patrons with outstanding fines; exclude specified categories such as do-not-disturb, VIP, staff, or opted-out patrons; and export results to CSV. The report must support background processing and retrieval of completed results.

requirements.name: Consortium Scale Support
requirements.description: The system must support a library consortium with 286 locations, 17 million annual circulations, and purchasing or processing more than 900,000 items per year.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority.

requirements.name: Non-Disruptive Report Processing
requirements.description: The system must process searches and reports during open hours without disrupting other system functions, including circulation and patron access to the OPAC. Long-running reports must be capable of background processing or other isolation from operational activity.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks the open-hours operating requirement High Priority.

requirements.name: Server Operating Environment
requirements.description: The system must operate on Linux or Solaris servers, including the Linux and Solaris environments used for production and disaster recovery.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority.

requirements.name: Client Access Platforms
requirements.description: The system must be accessible through a web browser or a Windows-compatible client.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority.

requirements.name: Supported Web Browsers
requirements.description: When accessed through a web browser, the system must support Microsoft Internet Explorer version 6.0 or later and Mozilla Firefox version 2.0 or later.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this Medium Priority.

requirements.name: Assistive Technology Access
requirements.description: The system must support screen readers, screen-magnification software, and other assistive technologies, including JAWS, NVDA, and ZoomText, and comply with Section 508 accessibility requirements.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority; D16 calls accessibility non-negotiable and D18 calls Section 508 compliance mandatory.

requirements.name: Relational Database Support
requirements.description: The system must use and work with a fully relational database structure and support reporting queries across relational data. It must not require a denormalized reporting schema synchronized with the live database.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks the relational database requirement High Priority.

requirements.name: Standards-Compliant HTML
requirements.description: The system must produce standards-compliant HTML for web interfaces, help content, and report output.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority.

requirements.name: Separate System Environments
requirements.description: The system must provide separate development, training, and production environments. The training environment must allow staff to practice without risking production data, and configurations such as templates, permissions, and saved queries must be migratable into production.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks development and training environments with configuration migration Medium Priority.

requirements.name: Role-Based Access Control
requirements.description: The system must control user rights through security groups or roles assigned to individuals, workgroups, and staff groups, and allow administrators to manage permissions through role assignment. Roles must support access appropriate to staff, managers, local administrators, and global administrators.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority.

requirements.name: Preserve OPAC Functionality
requirements.description: Management reporting functionality must not constrain or adversely affect the functionality or performance of the Online Public Access Catalog.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority; D16 calls OPAC separation critical.

requirements.name: Record Data Specifications
requirements.description: Product documentation must provide complete data specifications for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold/request, and other records maintained or accessed by the Management Processes, including field names, data types, and relationships.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority.

requirements.name: Process Description Documentation
requirements.description: Product documentation must provide high-level descriptions of major processes, including bibliographic record import and export, validation against internal and external authority sources, and standard reports.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this Medium Priority.

requirements.name: Online System Help
requirements.description: The system must provide online HTML help that is hierarchical, cross-linked, and describes and illustrates system functions. Staff must be able to find help without leaving the system, and the help must be accessible to screen-reader users.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority.

requirements.name: Error Reporting and Feedback
requirements.description: The system must provide high-level error reporting and feedback and low-level query-specific feedback through the front-end interface for Local and Global System Administrators.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this Medium Priority.

requirements.name: Staff Login Methods
requirements.description: The system must support individual staff authentication using traditional username and password and an optional streamlined method such as an employee-card swipe. Card-based login must not be required or bypass individual authentication, and the system must identify which staff member is logged in.

requirements.name: Manage Report Templates
requirements.description: Administrators must be able to create report templates available to staff. Staff must be able to run templates as-is or modify only permitted selections, with changes preserving dependable results. Authorized users must also be able to create templates for PINES libraries and clone an existing template into a separate variant.

requirements.name: Administer Report Permissions
requirements.description: The system must provide fine-grained, role-administered permissions controlling who may create, clone, run, and access reports. Administrators must be able to create shared folders that allow or disallow access to specific reports and ad hoc reports on specified data sets.

requirements.name: Multi-Record Query Builder
requirements.description: The system must provide a user-friendly query-design interface for bibliographic, item, patron, transaction, and financial records. Users must be able to select fields, choose values from picklists, select regular expressions from a dropdown, and use Boolean operators; administrators must control staff access to tables and fields.

requirements.name: Executive Board Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide predefined reports for library boards and other external consumers, including basic statistics required by the Georgia Annual Report and Application for State Aid. Activity reports must include checkouts, check-ins, holds placed, and holds filled, with cross-tabulation by terminal, branch, system, hour, patron age range, patron type, and patron location.

requirements.name: Privacy-Protecting Transaction Archives
requirements.description: The system must archive transaction data for the period required by applicable law while protecting patron privacy by removing personally identifiable information and retaining useful demographic statistics.

requirements.name: Periodic Management Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide periodic management reports for bibliographic records with holds; items not checked out for a specified number of days; item-level holds; invalid item types; in-transit items with outstanding holds; last copies; long call numbers; missing items; bibliographic records without item records; and patrons with invalid home libraries.

requirements.name: Display Report Criteria
requirements.description: The system must display the query selections and clearly defined selection criteria with report results. Results must also identify the report name and selected date criteria.

requirements.name: Report Queue Visibility
requirements.description: Staff must be able to view their report's queue position, the number of reports ahead, submission time, and status, including waiting, running, completed, or failed.

requirements.name: Patron Behavior Statistics
requirements.description: The system must produce statistics for understanding and predicting patron behavior and material use, including average return speed for a particular book, likelihood of renewal, renewal rates, and the percentage of branch checkouts that are renewals.

requirements.name: Anonymized Demographic Statistics
requirements.description: The system must produce demographic statistics, including transactions by geographic region and age range, using anonymized data that does not identify individual patrons.

requirements.name: Uncataloged Material Inventory
requirements.description: The system must track uncataloged materials, including paperback books and children's board books, as inventory before individual catalog records are complete. It must support rapid distribution with minimal branch labor, identify material use, and include related transactions in circulation statistics and reports.

requirements.name: Transaction History Retention
requirements.description: The system must retain detailed transaction history for a configurable number of days and retain monthly and annual aggregate information indefinitely.

requirements.name: Group Transaction Reports
requirements.description: The system must group transactions by hour, terminal, branch, and system and support queries for all transactions or transaction types, including check-ins, checkouts, fines collected, and patron registrations.

requirements.name: Count Check-In Types
requirements.description: The system must count check-ins individually and cumulatively by method, including book drop, terminal, staff user, and self-service. Check-in date and time reporting must distinguish check-ins from renewals.

requirements.name: Count Check-Out Types
requirements.description: The system must count checkouts individually and cumulatively by staff checkout, self-checkout, staff renewal, self-checkout renewal, online renewal, and OPAC renewal.

requirements.name: Report Hold Placement Methods
requirements.description: The system must count hold requests and report how each hold was placed, including at a staff desk, at a public computer inside the library, or remotely.

requirements.name: Transaction Summary Reports
requirements.description: The system must report holds placed, holds filled, and checkouts per patron, library, selected group of libraries, system, or county. Reports must display checkout and placed-hold counts per patron and subtotal holds by type, including active, frozen, and frozen-until holds.

requirements.name: Collection Value Reports
requirements.description: The system must report item values based on item-record data for the entire collection or a selected portion, including items selected by status, format, collection, call number, or shelving location.

requirements.name: Financial Audit Compliance
requirements.description: The system's reports and archived data must comply with standard accounting practice and applicable state, county, and municipal auditing requirements.

requirements.name: Manage Patron Financial Data
requirements.description: The system must associate fines, charges, waivers, and ecommerce transactions with patron and item records; support financial queries joining those records; allow financial information to be updated and reflected promptly; track fines waived and payments by library; and allow users to query accounts above a specified balance.

requirements.name: Financial Reports
requirements.description: The system must report patron account balances by patron, home library, and system; fines and charges by time period and charge type; fines waived by time period and branch; and payments by time period, payment method, and collecting library.

requirements.name: Payment Audit Ledger
requirements.description: The system must maintain a ledger of patron payments identifying the specific charges to which each payment was applied, so finance staff can trace payments and reconcile accounts.
requirements.source_priority_note: D11 calls the financial audit trail critical.

requirements.name: Circulation Report Catalogue
requirements.description: The system must provide circulation reports for check-in and checkout counts; overdue items with relevant contact information; circulation by modifier, category, Dewey classification, shelving location, MARC fields, patron county, home library, and age; renewals; non-cataloged circulation; and total circulation, including combined cataloged and non-cataloged counts.

requirements.name: Item Report Catalogue
requirements.description: The system must provide item reports for items added, deleted, edited, counted, currently checked out, overdue, long overdue, missing, in transit, claimed returned, or created within a date range; items selected by use count or fines-stopped reason; weeding information; last copies deleted; and collection age or value by call number or shelving location.

requirements.name: Bibliographic Report Catalogue
requirements.description: The system must report bibliographic-record counts, edited-record counts, records added by user and library, records without attached volumes, and records missing specified MARC fields.

requirements.name: Patron Report Catalogue
requirements.description: The system must provide reports for patron counts and additions; patrons by demographic category, age, county, city, ZIP code, home library, profile group, survey response, expiration date, inactive or barred status, and note wording; voter survey responses; and staff accounts by password-change date and account expiration.

requirements.name: Hold Report Catalogue
requirements.description: The system must provide reports for hold purchase alerts, items sent or received for holds, IntraPINES loans by system or facility, unfilled holds, annual hold counts, and stale holds awaiting pickup.

requirements.name: In-House Use Reports
requirements.description: The system must report non-cataloged in-house use counts by month and cataloged in-house use counts.

requirements.name: Bills Report Catalogue
requirements.description: The system must provide reports for bills currently owed by patrons, detailed payments received, detailed forgive/work/goods payments, detailed voids, and aged debt.

requirements.name: Canned Report Interface
requirements.description: The system must provide generic canned reports that users can run immediately or schedule to run ASAP, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly. Users must be able to select multiple reports to run together and view their results in one document.

requirements.name: On-Demand Report Interface
requirements.description: The system must provide an on-demand reporting interface for preset maintenance, collection-development, and similar reports, allowing users to edit selection criteria and display options before execution.

requirements.name: Open Template Reporting
requirements.description: The system must provide open-template reporting with circulation, item, patron, bill, and bibliographic attributes available for filtering and display.

requirements.name: Report Output Formats
requirements.description: The system must provide reports in Excel, HTML, CSV, and pivot-table formats.

requirements.name: Email Report Delivery
requirements.description: The system must allow users to deliver reports by email, enter recipients, and select recipients from an address book of regularly used addresses.

requirements.name: Edit Recurring Reports
requirements.description: Users must be able to edit recurring reports by adding or removing report selections and changing the report's email recipients.

requirements.name: Comparative Report Columns
requirements.description: The system must support report outputs with comparative columns for periods such as last month's circulation, the previous month's circulation, percentage difference, the corresponding month of the previous year, and percentage difference between those periods.

requirements.name: Edit Canned Report Displays
requirements.description: Authorized users must be able to add canned reports according to their permissions and edit canned-report display fields, such as adding shelving location.

requirements.name: Prioritize Report Queue
requirements.description: The system must allow designated report types, such as board reports, to be prioritized ahead of lower-priority or resource-consuming reports in the execution queue.

requirements.name: Item Usage Reports
requirements.description: The system must report total item-use counts and counts for selected date ranges, including fiscal-year and monthly use, and provide last-circulation dates and weeding data such as date of last circulation and circulation count.

requirements.name: Upload Report Filters
requirements.description: Users must be able to upload a text file containing values such as barcodes or TCNs and use those values to filter a report.

requirements.name: Notice Activity Reports
requirements.description: The system must support reports on pre-overdue notices, overdue notices, and holds notices sent.

requirements.name: Cancel Report Execution
requirements.description: Users must be able to cancel a report that is scheduled or currently running.

requirements.name: Real-Time Reporting
requirements.description: The system must support reports using current data in real time, including reports used to monitor current activity.

requirements.name: Historical Reporting
requirements.description: The system must support reporting on data as it existed at a specified prior date or date range, including historical shelving locations and snapshots of bills. This reporting capability does not prescribe a particular storage architecture.

requirements.name: Filter Surveys By Name
requirements.description: Users must be able to select a survey by its name rather than entering its identifier, and the system must resolve the name to the corresponding survey record.

requirements.name: Single-Row MARC Reporting
requirements.description: The system must extract selected MARC fields for reports and display those fields on a single row of report data, including when the fields are stored across multiple rows.

requirements.name: Workstation Transaction Reports
requirements.description: The system must report transactions by specified date and time, workstation, or staff member to support analysis of activity and staff workflow.

requirements.name: Enforce Archive Retention
requirements.description: The system must enforce data-archiving retention policies required for audits, including a seven-year retention period where applicable under state and local requirements.

requirements.name: Item Edit Date Reporting
requirements.description: Item reports must show the last edit date based on item edits only; circulation activity must not change or be included in that date.

requirements.name: Data Quality Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide reports identifying data-quality problems, including items with invalid item types or excessively long call numbers and bibliographic records without item records.

requirements.name: Detailed Aged Debt Report
requirements.description: The system must provide an aged-debt report with detailed debt information.

requirements.name: Prevent Duplicate Export Rows
requirements.description: Report exports must avoid unintended duplicate rows so exported data can be used without repeated records.

requirements.name: Vendor Data Integration
requirements.description: The system must support data exchange with vendor websites through published APIs or automated transfers of standard-format data files, including USMARC21 and EDIFACT, while accommodating locations where particular vendor data is unavailable.

glossary.definition: A library location within a library system or consortium.
A group of library systems or locations sharing the library automation and management reporting environment.
A physical library copy represented by an item record.
Machine-Readable Cataloging, the record format used to represent bibliographic data.
The Online Public Access Catalog through which patrons access library catalog services.
A person who uses a library's resources or services.
A reusable report definition with specified selection criteria and display options.

blacklist.name: Efficient Batch Processing
blacklist.description: The system must process batch location updates efficiently for an inventory of approximately 9.6 million items and avoid database locking problems by processing updates in smaller batches.
blacklist.reason: The candidate prescribes implementation and performance handling (smaller batches and avoidance of database locking) rather than a distinct user-facing capability or testable system quality. D04 mentions this only as a technical concern; the transfer capability is retained separately.

blacklist.name: Report Output Validation
blacklist.description: Report output must be tested and proven accurate for its intended reporting purpose.
blacklist.reason: This is a testing and QA process, not a capability or quality stated as a product behavior. D10's specification text calls for tested and proven output, but the candidate does not define a testable product requirement.

blacklist.name: Centralized Multi-Location Service
blacklist.description: Management Processes must be consolidated at a central location that accepts input from and provides services to multiple library locations, supporting a single source of truth for reporting.
blacklist.reason: D19 labels central consolidation as an assumption rather than a required system capability; the source does not make this an explicit product requirement.

blacklist.name: Enterprise ILS Integration
blacklist.description: The management processes must use the data structures and functionality of an enterprise-level Library Automation System, including its Acquisitions and Cataloging modules, rather than independently managing those functions.
blacklist.reason: D18 presents this as an assumption and dependency on the enterprise library system, not as a capability required of the reporting product.

blacklist.name: Library Automation Integration
blacklist.description: Management Processes must rely on and read the data structures and functionality of the enterprise-level Library Automation System, including its Acquisitions and Cataloging modules, without managing acquisitions or cataloging data.
blacklist.reason: D19 presents this as an assumption and dependency on the enterprise library system, not as a capability required of the reporting product.

requirements.name: Revert Transferred Items
requirements.description: The system must automatically or manually return transferred items to their original locations after a configured period or when configured criteria are met. Supported criteria include time-based conditions and item-status or destination events; the sources do not establish whether checkout at the destination should trigger reversion.
requirements.source_priority_note: D04 calls automatic reversion important

requirements.name: Transfer History Records
requirements.description: The system must retain transfer activity for audit and expose item transfer history so staff can review completed and reverted transfers and determine how often an item has moved.

requirements.name: Print Transit Labels
requirements.description: The system must generate printable transit labels containing barcodes for items being transferred.

requirements.name: Restrict Transfer Permissions
requirements.description: The system must restrict item transfers to authorized roles, including managers, administrators, or transfer coordinators, and prevent unauthorized staff from performing transfers.

requirements.name: Alert Transfer Problems
requirements.description: The system must notify responsible staff when an item transfer is delayed or encounters an issue.

requirements.name: Missing Damaged Items Report
requirements.description: The system must provide a report of missing and damaged items by branch. The report must include item condition notes and support date ranges for trend analysis.

requirements.name: Delayed Transit Items Report
requirements.description: The system must generate one report of items that have remained in transit longer than a configurable number of days, with views per branch and system-wide. The report must combine transit-to and transit-from items, identify items with no arrival date and an overdue departure date, and allow sorting by due date. Seven days is suggested as the default threshold.

requirements.name: Transit Location Reports
requirements.description: The system must report items in transit by sending library and destination library, and provide reports of items currently in transit between locations for delivery coordination.
requirements.source_priority_note: D18 records in-transit item reports as critical

requirements.name: Identify Purge Candidates
requirements.description: The system must identify item records eligible for purging using customizable, combinable criteria, including status (such as missing, discard/weed, or damaged), time spent in a status, and time since last circulation.
requirements.source_priority_note: D06 marks the last-copy report critical; this note does not apply to purge-candidate identification

requirements.name: Review Purge Candidates
requirements.description: The system must provide read-only reports of item records identified as purge candidates so users can review them without changing or deleting records through the reports.

requirements.name: Batch Status Conversion
requirements.description: The system must support converting multiple items from one status to another in a batch, such as changing items from missing to discard/weed, and provide a report or workflow to assist with the conversion.

requirements.name: Last Copy Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide last-copy reports identifying items that are the only copy within a selected scope, including an individual library and the entire consortium. Reports must also identify deleted items that were the last copy in a library system or facility, supporting catalogers' WorldCat updates.
requirements.source_priority_note: D06 marks the last-copy report critical; D15 calls it critical

requirements.name: Delete Volumes With Copies
requirements.description: The system must provide a method to delete volume entries together with their associated copy entries during collection cleanup.

requirements.name: Delete Itemless Records
requirements.description: The system must provide a method to delete records that have no items attached during collection cleanup.

requirements.name: Confirm Purge Deletions
requirements.description: The system must require a separate confirmation step before executing purge deletions, distinct from identifying and reviewing candidates.

requirements.name: Audit Record Deletions
requirements.description: The system must retain an audit record of successful deletions, including record type, record identifier, timestamp, user, and user location. This tracking must cover purge activity and other record deletions.

requirements.name: Track Denied Deletions
requirements.description: The system must track deletion attempts that are denied so administrators can identify attempted deletions of records that users should not delete.

requirements.name: Report Deletion Activity
requirements.description: The system must report deletion activity for a selected period, including totals and breakdowns by record type, location, system, and user, and identify users with the highest deletion counts.

requirements.name: Filter Patron Reports
requirements.description: The system must allow patron queries and reports to be limited by age range, ZIP code, county of residence, home branch, patron type, and preferred language. Users must be able to combine these filters with other conditions using AND and OR logic.
requirements.source_priority_note: D08 describes these reports as essential for program planning

requirements.name: Group Patron Reports
requirements.description: The system must group patron queries and reports by age range, ZIP code, county of residence, home branch, patron type, and preferred language, and show aggregates such as circulation counts and patron counts for each group.
requirements.source_priority_note: D08 describes these reports as essential for program planning

requirements.name: Configure Patron Age Ranges
requirements.description: The system must allow age ranges used for patron filtering and grouping to be configured for each report and calculated from patrons' birth dates. Configurations must support user-defined brackets such as 0–5, 6–10, and 11–15.

requirements.name: Include Null Report Values
requirements.description: Report results must include records with null or blank values rather than silently excluding them, including patrons with unpopulated optional demographic fields.

requirements.name: Inactive Patron Reports
requirements.description: The system must generate lists of patrons with no circulation or electronic activity during a configurable number of days. Electronic activity includes account or OPAC logins, online holds, online renewals, and logged access to integrated digital collections. Users must be able to select System, Home Library, County, or another required organizational level; include current mailing addresses; separately identify patrons with outstanding fines; exclude specified categories such as do-not-disturb, VIP, staff, or opted-out patrons; and export results to CSV. The report must support background processing and retrieval of completed results.

requirements.name: Consortium Scale Support
requirements.description: The system must support a library consortium with 286 locations, 17 million annual circulations, and purchasing or processing more than 900,000 items per year.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority

requirements.name: Non-Disruptive Report Processing
requirements.description: The system must process searches and reports during open hours without disrupting other system functions, including circulation and patron access to the OPAC. Long-running reports must be capable of background processing or other isolation from operational activity.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks the open-hours operating requirement High Priority

requirements.name: Server Operating Environment
requirements.description: The system must operate on Linux or Solaris servers, including the Linux and Solaris environments used for production and disaster recovery.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority

requirements.name: Client Access Platforms
requirements.description: The system must be accessible through a web browser or a Windows-compatible client.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority

requirements.name: Supported Web Browsers
requirements.description: When accessed through a web browser, the system must support Microsoft Internet Explorer version 6.0 or later and Mozilla Firefox version 2.0 or later.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this Medium Priority

requirements.name: Assistive Technology Access
requirements.description: The system must support screen readers, screen-magnification software, and other assistive technologies, including JAWS, NVDA, and ZoomText, and comply with Section 508 accessibility requirements.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority; D16 calls accessibility non-negotiable and D18 calls Section 508 compliance mandatory

requirements.name: Relational Database Support
requirements.description: The system must use and work with a fully relational database structure and support reporting queries across relational data. It must not require a denormalized reporting schema synchronized with the live database.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks the relational database requirement High Priority

requirements.name: Standards-Compliant HTML
requirements.description: The system must produce standards-compliant HTML for web interfaces, help content, and report output.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority

requirements.name: Separate System Environments
requirements.description: The system must provide separate development, training, and production environments. The training environment must allow staff to practice without risking production data, and configurations such as templates, permissions, and saved queries must be migratable into production.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks development and training environments with configuration migration Medium Priority

requirements.name: Role-Based Access Control
requirements.description: The system must control user rights through security groups or roles assigned to individuals, workgroups, and staff groups, and allow administrators to manage permissions through role assignment. Roles must support access appropriate to staff, managers, local administrators, and global administrators.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority

requirements.name: Preserve OPAC Functionality
requirements.description: Management reporting functionality must not constrain or adversely affect the functionality or performance of the Online Public Access Catalog.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority; D16 calls OPAC separation critical

requirements.name: Record Data Specifications
requirements.description: Product documentation must provide complete data specifications for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold/request, and other records maintained or accessed by the Management Processes, including field names, data types, and relationships.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority

requirements.name: Process Description Documentation
requirements.description: Product documentation must provide high-level descriptions of major processes, including bibliographic record import and export, validation against internal and external authority sources, and standard reports.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this Medium Priority

requirements.name: Online System Help
requirements.description: The system must provide online HTML help that is hierarchical, cross-linked, and describes and illustrates system functions. Staff must be able to find help without leaving the system, and the help must be accessible to screen-reader users.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority

requirements.name: Error Reporting and Feedback
requirements.description: The system must provide high-level error reporting and feedback and low-level query-specific feedback through the front-end interface for Local and Global System Administrators.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks this Medium Priority

requirements.name: Staff Login Methods
requirements.description: The system must support individual staff authentication using traditional username and password and an optional streamlined method such as an employee-card swipe. Card-based login must not be required or bypass individual authentication, and the system must identify which staff member is logged in.

requirements.name: Manage Report Templates
requirements.description: Administrators must be able to create report templates available to staff. Staff must be able to run templates as-is or modify only permitted selections, with changes preserving dependable results. Authorized users must also be able to create templates for PINES libraries and clone an existing template into a separate variant.

requirements.name: Administer Report Permissions
requirements.description: The system must provide fine-grained, role-administered permissions controlling who may create, clone, run, and access reports. Administrators must be able to create shared folders that allow or disallow access to specific reports and ad hoc reports on specified data sets.

requirements.name: Multi-Record Query Builder
requirements.description: The system must provide a user-friendly query-design interface for bibliographic, item, patron, transaction, and financial records. Users must be able to select fields, choose values from picklists, select regular expressions from a dropdown, and use Boolean operators; administrators must control staff access to tables and fields.

requirements.name: Executive Board Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide predefined reports for library boards and other external consumers, including basic statistics required by the Georgia Annual Report and Application for State Aid. Activity reports must include checkouts, check-ins, holds placed, and holds filled, with cross-tabulation by terminal, branch, system, hour, patron age range, patron type, and patron location.

requirements.name: Privacy-Protecting Transaction Archives
requirements.description: The system must archive transaction data for the period required by applicable law while protecting patron privacy by removing personally identifiable information and retaining useful demographic statistics.
requirements.source_priority_note: D12 states that State law requires this transaction retention and privacy protection for compliance

requirements.name: Periodic Management Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide periodic management reports for bibliographic records with holds; items not checked out for a specified number of days; item-level holds; invalid item types; in-transit items with outstanding holds; last copies; long call numbers; missing items; bibliographic records without item records; and patrons with invalid home libraries.

requirements.name: Display Report Criteria
requirements.description: The system must display the query selections and clearly defined selection criteria with report results. Results must also identify the report name and selected date criteria.

requirements.name: Report Queue Visibility
requirements.description: Staff must be able to view their report's queue position, the number of reports ahead, submission time, and status, including waiting, running, completed, or failed.

requirements.name: Patron Behavior Statistics
requirements.description: The system must produce statistics for understanding and predicting patron behavior and material use, including average return speed for a particular book, likelihood of renewal, renewal rates, and the percentage of branch checkouts that are renewals.

requirements.name: Anonymized Demographic Statistics
requirements.description: The system must produce demographic statistics, including transactions by geographic region and age range, using anonymized data that does not identify individual patrons.

requirements.name: Uncataloged Material Inventory
requirements.description: The system must track uncataloged materials, including paperback books and children's board books, as inventory before individual catalog records are complete. It must support rapid distribution with minimal branch labor, identify material use, and include related transactions in circulation statistics and reports.

requirements.name: Transaction History Retention
requirements.description: The system must retain detailed transaction history for a configurable number of days and retain monthly and annual aggregate information indefinitely.

requirements.name: Group Transaction Reports
requirements.description: The system must group transactions by hour, terminal, branch, and system and support queries for all transactions or transaction types, including check-ins, checkouts, fines collected, and patron registrations.

requirements.name: Count Check-In Types
requirements.description: The system must count check-ins individually and cumulatively by method, including book drop, terminal, staff user, and self-service. Check-in date and time reporting must distinguish check-ins from renewals.

requirements.name: Count Check-Out Types
requirements.description: The system must count checkouts individually and cumulatively by staff checkout, self-checkout, staff renewal, self-checkout renewal, online renewal, and OPAC renewal.

requirements.name: Report Hold Placement Methods
requirements.description: The system must count hold requests and report how each hold was placed, including at a staff desk, at a public computer inside the library, or remotely.

requirements.name: Transaction Summary Reports
requirements.description: The system must report holds placed, holds filled, and checkouts per patron, library, selected group of libraries, system, or county. Reports must display checkout and placed-hold counts per patron and subtotal holds by type, including active, frozen, and frozen-until holds.

requirements.name: Collection Value Reports
requirements.description: The system must report item values based on item-record data for the entire collection or a selected portion, including items selected by status, format, collection, call number, or shelving location.

requirements.name: Financial Audit Compliance
requirements.description: The system's reports and archived data must comply with standard accounting practice and applicable state, county, and municipal auditing requirements.

requirements.name: Manage Patron Financial Data
requirements.description: The system must associate fines, charges, waivers, and ecommerce transactions with patron and item records; support financial queries joining those records; allow financial information to be updated and reflected promptly; track fines waived and payments by library; and allow users to query accounts above a specified balance.

requirements.name: Financial Reports
requirements.description: The system must report patron account balances by patron, home library, and system; fines and charges by time period and charge type; fines waived by time period and branch; and payments by time period, payment method, and collecting library.

requirements.name: Payment Audit Ledger
requirements.description: The system must maintain a ledger of patron payments identifying the specific charges to which each payment was applied, so finance staff can trace payments and reconcile accounts.
requirements.source_priority_note: D11 calls the financial audit trail critical

requirements.name: Circulation Report Catalogue
requirements.description: The system must provide circulation reports for check-in and checkout counts; overdue items with relevant contact information; circulation by modifier, category, Dewey classification, shelving location, MARC fields, patron county, home library, and age; renewals; non-cataloged circulation; and total circulation, including combined cataloged and non-cataloged counts.

requirements.name: Item Report Catalogue
requirements.description: The system must provide item reports for items added, deleted, edited, counted, currently checked out, overdue, long overdue, missing, in transit, claimed returned, or created within a date range; items selected by use count or fines-stopped reason; weeding information; last copies deleted; and collection age or value by call number or shelving location.

requirements.name: Bibliographic Report Catalogue
requirements.description: The system must report bibliographic-record counts, edited-record counts, records added by user and library, records without attached volumes, and records missing specified MARC fields.

requirements.name: Patron Report Catalogue
requirements.description: The system must provide reports for patron counts and additions; patrons by demographic category, age, county, city, ZIP code, home library, profile group, survey response, expiration date, inactive or barred status, and note wording; voter survey responses; and staff accounts by password-change date and account expiration.

requirements.name: Hold Report Catalogue
requirements.description: The system must provide reports for hold purchase alerts, items sent or received for holds, IntraPINES loans by system or facility, unfilled holds, annual hold counts, and stale holds awaiting pickup.

requirements.name: In-House Use Reports
requirements.description: The system must report non-cataloged in-house use counts by month and cataloged in-house use counts.

requirements.name: Bills Report Catalogue
requirements.description: The system must provide reports for bills currently owed by patrons, detailed payments received, detailed forgive/work/goods payments, detailed voids, and aged debt.

requirements.name: Canned Report Interface
requirements.description: The system must provide generic canned reports that users can run immediately or schedule to run ASAP, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly. Users must be able to select multiple reports to run together and view their results in one document.

requirements.name: On-Demand Report Interface
requirements.description: The system must provide an on-demand reporting interface for preset maintenance, collection-development, and similar reports, allowing users to edit selection criteria and display options before execution.

requirements.name: Open Template Reporting
requirements.description: The system must provide open-template reporting with circulation, item, patron, bill, and bibliographic attributes available for filtering and display.

requirements.name: Report Output Formats
requirements.description: The system must provide reports in Excel, HTML, CSV, and pivot-table formats.

requirements.name: Email Report Delivery
requirements.description: The system must allow users to deliver reports by email, enter recipients, and select recipients from an address book of regularly used addresses.

requirements.name: Edit Recurring Reports
requirements.description: Users must be able to edit recurring reports by adding or removing report selections and changing the report's email recipients.

requirements.name: Comparative Report Columns
requirements.description: The system must support report outputs with comparative columns for periods such as last month's circulation, the previous month's circulation, percentage difference, the corresponding month of the previous year, and percentage difference between those periods.

requirements.name: Edit Canned Report Displays
requirements.description: Authorized users must be able to add canned reports according to their permissions and edit canned-report display fields, such as adding shelving location.

requirements.name: Prioritize Report Queue
requirements.description: The system must allow designated report types, such as board reports, to be prioritized ahead of lower-priority or resource-consuming reports in the execution queue.
requirements.source_priority_note: D12 describes report prioritization as crucial and states that important reports should be able to jump the queue

requirements.name: Item Usage Reports
requirements.description: The system must report total item-use counts and counts for selected date ranges, including fiscal-year and monthly use, and provide last-circulation dates and weeding data such as date of last circulation and circulation count.

requirements.name: Upload Report Filters
requirements.description: Users must be able to upload a text file containing values such as barcodes or TCNs and use those values to filter a report.

requirements.name: Notice Activity Reports
requirements.description: The system must support reports on pre-overdue notices, overdue notices, and holds notices sent.

requirements.name: Cancel Report Execution
requirements.description: Users must be able to cancel a report that is scheduled or currently running.

requirements.name: Real-Time Reporting
requirements.description: The system must support reports using current data in real time, including reports used to monitor current activity.

requirements.name: Historical Reporting
requirements.description: The system must support reporting on data as it existed at a specified prior date or date range, including historical shelving locations and snapshots of bills. This reporting capability does not prescribe a particular storage architecture.

requirements.name: Filter Surveys By Name
requirements.description: Users must be able to select a survey by its name rather than entering its identifier, and the system must resolve the name to the corresponding survey record.

requirements.name: Single-Row MARC Reporting
requirements.description: The system must extract selected MARC fields for reports and display those fields on a single row of report data, including when the fields are stored across multiple rows.

requirements.name: Workstation Transaction Reports
requirements.description: The system must report transactions by specified date and time, workstation, or staff member to support analysis of activity and staff workflow.

requirements.name: Enforce Archive Retention
requirements.description: The system must enforce data-archiving retention policies required for audits, including a seven-year retention period where applicable under state and local requirements.

requirements.name: Item Edit Date Reporting
requirements.description: Item reports must show the last edit date based on item edits only; circulation activity must not change or be included in that date.

requirements.name: Data Quality Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide reports identifying data-quality problems, including items with invalid item types or excessively long call numbers and bibliographic records without item records.

requirements.name: Detailed Aged Debt Report
requirements.description: The system must provide an aged-debt report with detailed debt information.

requirements.name: Prevent Duplicate Export Rows
requirements.description: Report exports must avoid unintended duplicate rows so exported data can be used without repeated records.

requirements.name: Vendor Data Integration
requirements.description: The system must support data exchange with vendor websites through published APIs or automated transfers of standard-format data files, including USMARC21 and EDIFACT, while accommodating locations where particular vendor data is unavailable.

requirement.name: Efficient Batch Processing
requirement.description: The system must process batch location updates efficiently for an inventory of approximately 9.6 million items and avoid database locking problems by processing updates in smaller batches.

blacklist.reason: The candidate prescribes implementation and performance handling (smaller batches and avoidance of database locking) rather than a distinct user-facing capability or testable system quality. D04 mentions this only as a technical concern; the transfer capability is retained separately.

requirement.name: Report Output Validation
requirement.description: Report output must be tested and proven accurate for its intended reporting purpose.

blacklist.reason: This is a testing and QA process, not a capability or quality stated as a product behavior. D10's specification text calls for tested and proven output, but the candidate does not define a testable product requirement.

requirement.name: Centralized Multi-Location Service
requirement.description: Management Processes must be consolidated at a central location that accepts input from and provides services to multiple library locations, supporting a single source of truth for reporting.

blacklist.reason: D19 labels central consolidation as an assumption rather than a required system capability; the source does not make this an explicit product requirement.

requirement.name: Enterprise ILS Integration
requirement.description: The management processes must use the data structures and functionality of an enterprise-level Library Automation System, including its Acquisitions and Cataloging modules, rather than independently managing those functions.

blacklist.reason: D18 presents this as an assumption and dependency on the enterprise library system, not as a capability required of the reporting product.

requirement.name: Library Automation Integration
requirement.description: Management Processes must rely on and read the data structures and functionality of the enterprise-level Library Automation System, including its Acquisitions and Cataloging modules, without managing acquisitions or cataloging data.

blacklist.reason: D19 presents this as an assumption and dependency on the enterprise library system, not as a capability required of the reporting product.

glossary.definition: A library location within a library system or consortium.
A group of library systems or locations sharing the library automation and management reporting environment.
A physical library copy represented by an item record.
Machine-Readable Cataloging, the record format used to represent bibliographic data.
The Online Public Access Catalog through which patrons access library catalog services.
A person who uses a library's resources or services.
A reusable report definition with specified selection criteria and display options.

open_questions.question: What specific metrics or configured limits define branch capacity?
How should shelf space be estimated when measurements are not directly tracked: from item dimensions, item count, or another method?
Should checkout at a transfer destination trigger automatic reversion, or should checked-out items remain there while unused items revert?
What threshold should be used for the delayed in-transit report beyond the suggested configurable default of seven days?
Which electronic activities count toward inactivity when digital-resource access is not integrated or logged?
How many years must transaction data be retained under applicable State law?

messages.content:
You place candidate requirements that the consolidation step left unassigned. The user message is JSON with numbered "candidates" (index, name, description, source document) and the numbered current "requirements" (index, name, one-line description).

For every candidate return exactly one item, with no missing or duplicate indices:
- maps_to = the index of the requirement that already covers it (a tester would write one test for both, or the candidate is only a detail of that requirement) and new = false; or
- new = true and maps_to = null when no current requirement covers it.
Map only when the coverage is genuine; a shared topic is not coverage.

Definition of a requirement: A requirement describes one capability, rule or quality the system must provide, at the level a tester would write one acceptance test for. It names what, for whom, and under what condition, and it is independent of how it is implemented. Two statements are the same requirement if a tester would write one test for both. A statement is too broad if its acceptance test would have to be several unrelated tests. A statement is too narrow if it only makes sense as a detail of another requirement, such as one filter option of a report.

Example of a statement that is too broad: "Staff can manage item transfers between branches, including selecting candidate items by circulation history and keeping an audit history of every completed transfer." This is exactly two requirements: (1) select transfer candidates by circulation history, (2) record an audit history of completed transfers.
Example of statements that are too narrow: "The inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch" and "The inactive patron report can be filtered by patron profile". These are one requirement: the inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch and patron profile.

added.name: Configuration Migration
added.description: The reporting system must support migration of configuration between environments.

added.name: Configuration Migration
added.description: The system must provide export and import functionality to migrate configurations developed in development or training into production, including report templates, permission settings, and other configuration.

added.name: Read-Only OPAC Data Access
added.description: Management Processes must interact with the OPAC patron interface by querying data such as holds and circulation transactions, without modifying that data.

messages.content:
You assign priorities to software requirements. The user message is JSON with "fixed" requirements whose priority is already decided (for calibration only, do not output them) and numbered "items" that need a priority.

Priority scale:
- High: Core to the system's purpose or requested by many stakeholders; the system is not acceptable without it.
- Medium: Clearly valuable and requested, but the system can go live without it and add it in a later release.
- Low: Nice to have, requested by a single stakeholder or marginal to the core workflows; implement only if time allows.

Hard rule, applied first: if an item's source_priority_note reports an explicit priority marker in a specification document (for example [*] or High in a draft SRS), a source calling the item critical, or wording that it is legally required, mandatory, non-negotiable or a compliance obligation, the priority is High and the justification names that source. An individual's emphasis in an e-mail or interview ("crucial", "essential", "we really need") is evidence for the judgment below, not a trigger.

Judge every other item by how central it is to the system's purpose, how many source documents ask for it (source_doc_ids) and whether the system can work without it, calibrated against the fixed requirements:
- Medium is not a default: clear value without urgency is Medium; nice-to-have and single-stakeholder conveniences are Low. Aim for a defensible spread across the three levels.
- A feature mentioned once in passing by one person is not High on its own, nor is a requirement that only exists as a thin list heading (for example "provide canned reports").
- A sub-feature of a report or utility is never higher than the report or utility.

Return exactly one entry per numbered item, with no missing or duplicate indices. justification is one sentence that agrees with the level: a justification that calls the item essential, critical, fundamental or mandatory belongs to a High item, Medium justifications describe clear value without urgency, Low ones a nice-to-have. It is not circular: instead of "X is essential", say who depends on it, what fails without it, or which signal in the sources decided it.
