outputs.priority_justification: The requirement explicitly calls for compliance with applicable state, county, and municipal auditing requirements, so financial reporting must meet those obligations.

outputs.name: Multi-Record Query Builder
outputs.description: The system must provide a user-friendly query-design interface for bibliographic, item, patron, transaction, and financial records. Users must be able to select fields, choose values from picklists, select regular expressions from a dropdown, and use Boolean operators; administrators must control staff access to tables and fields.
outputs.priority_justification: A multi-record query builder provides a broad way to create reports across core library data, requested in three sources and central to the reporting platform.

outputs.name: Non-Disruptive Report Processing
outputs.description: The system must process searches and reports during open hours without disrupting other system functions, including circulation and patron access to the OPAC. Long-running reports must be capable of background processing or other isolation from operational activity.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 marks open-hours report processing High Priority, and D14, D16, and D18 also address avoiding disruption to live services.
outputs.source_priority_note: D10 marks the open-hours operating requirement High Priority

outputs.name: Online System Help
outputs.description: The system must provide online HTML help that is hierarchical, cross-linked, and describes and illustrates system functions. Staff must be able to find help without leaving the system, and the help must be accessible to screen-reader users.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 marks online system help High Priority, and the requirement is repeated across five sources, including accessibility for screen-reader users.
outputs.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority

outputs.name: Payment Audit Ledger
outputs.description: The system must maintain a ledger of patron payments identifying the specific charges to which each payment was applied, so finance staff can trace payments and reconcile accounts.
outputs.priority_justification: D11 calls the financial audit trail critical, and finance staff need payment-to-charge detail to trace and reconcile accounts.
outputs.source_priority_note: D11 calls the financial audit trail critical

outputs.name: Preserve OPAC Functionality
outputs.description: Management reporting functionality must not constrain or adversely affect the functionality or performance of the Online Public Access Catalog.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 marks OPAC preservation High Priority, and D16 calls separation from OPAC functionality critical because reporting must not impair patron access.
outputs.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority; D16 calls OPAC separation critical

outputs.name: Privacy-Protecting Transaction Archives
outputs.description: The system must archive transaction data for the period required by applicable law while protecting patron privacy by removing personally identifiable information and retaining useful demographic statistics.
outputs.priority_justification: D12 states that State law requires transaction retention and privacy protection, making the archive behavior a compliance obligation.
outputs.source_priority_note: D12 states that State law requires this transaction retention and privacy protection for compliance

outputs.name: Record Data Specifications
outputs.description: Product documentation must provide complete data specifications for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold/request, and other records maintained or accessed by the Management Processes, including field names, data types, and relationships.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 marks complete record data specifications High Priority, and these details support administration and interpretation across the system's record types.
outputs.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority

outputs.name: Relational Database Support
outputs.description: The system must use and work with a fully relational database structure and support reporting queries across relational data. It must not require a denormalized reporting schema synchronized with the live database.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 marks relational database support High Priority, and the requirement is repeated across four sources for reporting against relational data.
outputs.source_priority_note: D10 marks the relational database requirement High Priority

outputs.name: Role-Based Access Control
outputs.description: The system must control user rights through security groups or roles assigned to individuals, workgroups, and staff groups, and allow administrators to manage permissions through role assignment. Roles must support access appropriate to staff, managers, local administrators, and global administrators.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 marks role-based access High Priority, and the requirement is repeated in several sources for controlling staff and administrator permissions.
outputs.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority

outputs.name: Server Operating Environment
outputs.description: The system must operate on Linux or Solaris servers, including the Linux and Solaris environments used for production and disaster recovery.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 marks Linux or Solaris operation High Priority, and D16 and D18 also specify those server environments.
outputs.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority

outputs.name: Standards-Compliant HTML
outputs.description: The system must produce standards-compliant HTML for web interfaces, help content, and report output.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 marks standards-compliant HTML High Priority, with three other sources also specifying the output requirement.
outputs.source_priority_note: D10 marks this High Priority

outputs.name: Transit Location Reports
outputs.description: The system must report items in transit by sending library and destination library, and provide reports of items currently in transit between locations for delivery coordination.
outputs.priority_justification: D18 explicitly records in-transit item reports as critical, and delivery coordination depends on knowing sending and destination locations.
outputs.source_priority_note: D18 records in-transit item reports as critical

outputs.name: Enforce Archive Retention
outputs.description: The system must enforce data-archiving retention policies required for audits, including a seven-year retention period where applicable under state and local requirements.
outputs.priority_justification: The requirement specifies retention periods required for audits, including seven years where state and local rules apply, making enforcement a compliance obligation.

outputs.name: Read-Only OPAC Data Access
outputs.description: Management Processes must interact with the OPAC patron interface by querying data such as holds and circulation transactions, without modifying that data.
outputs.priority_justification: Read-only OPAC access protects patron-facing holds and circulation data from management-process changes, aligning with the multi-source requirement to preserve OPAC functionality.

outputs.name: Material Volume Reporting
outputs.description: The system must report material volume for a specified library at the current time or a selected historical point, separating new acquisitions, items on the shelf, items in circulation, and totals. Users must be able to break results down by categories such as total items, holds, adult fiction, and board books, customize categories, and report volume added in periods such as the last 30, 60, or 90 days.
outputs.priority_justification: The reports support collection planning, but the system can provide its broader reporting workflows without every requested volume breakdown.
outputs.source_priority_note: D01 calls this a key requirement

outputs.name: Branch Capacity Interface
outputs.description: The system must provide authorized users, including branch managers, an overview of capacity across all branches, with the ability to drill into individual branches, sort and filter by region, library type, and current load, view growth or shrinkage trends, and export the information to CSV. The capacity measure itself remains to be defined.
outputs.priority_justification: Branch managers gain useful capacity and trend visibility, though the capacity measure is still undefined and other management reporting can operate without it.

outputs.name: Shelf Space Usage Report
outputs.description: The system must compare, for each material genre and format, the percentage of total circulations, the percentage of the collection, and the percentage of total shelf space. Results must be available per library and system-wide, support date-range comparisons, and provide a side-by-side library comparison view. When shelf-space measurements are unavailable, the system must estimate shelf space using available item dimensions or item count as a proxy.
outputs.priority_justification: The comparisons help libraries make collection and shelf-space decisions, but they are a specialized analysis rather than a prerequisite for core reporting.

outputs.name: Generate Transfer Pull Lists
outputs.description: The system must generate printable pull lists identifying items selected for transfer so staff can retrieve them for movement.
outputs.priority_justification: Printable pull lists help staff retrieve selected items accurately, while transfers can still be coordinated through other procedures.

outputs.name: Preview Pending Transfers
outputs.description: Before applying a transfer, the system must show a preview of the proposed changes, including the number of items and their source and destination locations, and require confirmation before making the changes.
outputs.priority_justification: A preview and confirmation reduce accidental transfer changes, but they support rather than enable the system's broader workflows.

outputs.name: Query Transfer Candidates
outputs.description: The system must allow authorized staff to query for candidate materials for transfer or other administrative processing, using conditions such as material type, section, genre, or circulation history.
outputs.priority_justification: Candidate queries help staff identify materials for transfer and administrative work, but are one workflow within the broader system.

outputs.name: Restrict Transfer Permissions
outputs.description: The system must restrict item transfers to authorized roles, including managers, administrators, or transfer coordinators, and prevent unauthorized staff from performing transfers.
outputs.priority_justification: Role restrictions reduce the risk of unauthorized transfers, although this control applies to a narrower workflow than the system's general access management.

outputs.name: Revert Transferred Items
outputs.description: The system must automatically or manually return transferred items to their original locations after a configured period or when configured criteria are met. Supported criteria include time-based conditions and item-status or destination events; the sources do not establish whether checkout at the destination should trigger reversion.
outputs.priority_justification: Automatic or criteria-based reversion can reduce manual work for temporary transfers, though the sources leave some trigger behavior unresolved.
outputs.source_priority_note: D04 calls automatic reversion important

outputs.name: Save Reusable Queries
outputs.description: The system must allow users to save queries for repeated use, including recurring transfer and reporting tasks.
outputs.priority_justification: Reusable queries reduce repeated setup for recurring tasks, although users can still run those tasks by recreating queries.
outputs.source_priority_note: D04 calls saving queries for repeated use crucial

outputs.name: Select Transfer Results
outputs.description: The system must allow staff to manually select individual titles or items from query results, including selecting only part of a larger candidate set for subsequent administrative processing.
outputs.priority_justification: Selecting only relevant query results gives staff control over transfer batches, though the overall system can function without this refinement.

outputs.name: Transfer History Records
outputs.description: The system must retain transfer activity for audit and expose item transfer history so staff can review completed and reverted transfers and determine how often an item has moved.
outputs.priority_justification: Transfer history helps staff audit movements and answer item-history questions, but it is specific to the transfer utility.

outputs.name: Transfer Item Batches
outputs.description: The system must provide a utility for transferring batches of items between branches or other locations, including mobile libraries, outreach collections, warehouses, book sales, and event locations.
outputs.priority_justification: Batch transfers streamline moving materials across locations, while the wider management system can operate without this utility.

outputs.name: Update Item Locations
outputs.description: The system must allow authorized staff to change the location records of selected items to the transfer destination.
outputs.priority_justification: Updating locations completes the transfer workflow, but transfers are one operational utility among the system's broader reporting functions.

outputs.name: Delayed Transit Items Report
outputs.description: The system must generate one report of items that have remained in transit longer than a configurable number of days, with views per branch and system-wide. The report must combine transit-to and transit-from items, identify items with no arrival date and an overdue departure date, and allow sorting by due date. Seven days is suggested as the default threshold.
outputs.priority_justification: The report helps staff investigate overdue transit items, while the broader system can operate without this particular exception report.

outputs.name: Missing Damaged Items Report
outputs.description: The system must provide a report of missing and damaged items by branch. The report must include item condition notes and support date ranges for trend analysis.
outputs.priority_justification: Branch-level missing and damaged-item trends inform collection oversight, but this specialized report is not needed for other reporting workflows.

outputs.name: Audit Record Deletions
outputs.description: The system must retain an audit record of successful deletions, including record type, record identifier, timestamp, user, and user location. This tracking must cover purge activity and other record deletions.
outputs.priority_justification: Deletion audit records help administrators investigate changes across several source documents, but the system's reporting workflows can run without the audit feature.

outputs.name: Batch Status Conversion
outputs.description: The system must support converting multiple items from one status to another in a batch, such as changing items from missing to discard/weed, and provide a report or workflow to assist with the conversion.
outputs.priority_justification: Batch status conversion can reduce repetitive cleanup work, though staff can change statuses through other workflows.

outputs.name: Confirm Purge Deletions
outputs.description: The system must require a separate confirmation step before executing purge deletions, distinct from identifying and reviewing candidates.
outputs.priority_justification: A separate confirmation step helps prevent accidental purge deletions, but it supports rather than enables candidate identification and review.

outputs.name: Delete Itemless Records
outputs.description: The system must provide a method to delete records that have no items attached during collection cleanup.
outputs.priority_justification: Removing itemless records helps keep the catalog clean, although users can operate the reporting system without this cleanup method.

outputs.name: Delete Volumes With Copies
outputs.description: The system must provide a method to delete volume entries together with their associated copy entries during collection cleanup.
outputs.priority_justification: Deleting volumes with associated copies supports collection cleanup, but it is a specialized maintenance operation rather than a general reporting dependency.

outputs.name: Identify Purge Candidates
outputs.description: The system must identify item records eligible for purging using customizable, combinable criteria, including status (such as missing, discard/weed, or damaged), time spent in a status, and time since last circulation.
outputs.priority_justification: Customizable purge criteria help staff identify records for collection cleanup, but review and deletion workflows can be delivered separately.
outputs.source_priority_note: D06 marks the last-copy report critical; this note does not apply to purge-candidate identification

outputs.name: Filter Patron Reports
outputs.description: The system must allow patron queries and reports to be limited by age range, ZIP code, county of residence, home branch, patron type, and preferred language. Users must be able to combine these filters with other conditions using AND and OR logic.
outputs.priority_justification: These filters support patron-focused program planning, but the reports remain useful without every demographic and geographic selection.
outputs.source_priority_note: D08 describes these reports as essential for program planning

outputs.name: Group Patron Reports
outputs.description: The system must group patron queries and reports by age range, ZIP code, county of residence, home branch, patron type, and preferred language, and show aggregates such as circulation counts and patron counts for each group.
outputs.priority_justification: Grouping patron results helps organizations compare program reach, though it is a specialized analysis rather than a prerequisite for reporting.
outputs.source_priority_note: D08 describes these reports as essential for program planning

outputs.name: Include Null Report Values
outputs.description: Report results must include records with null or blank values rather than silently excluding them, including patrons with unpopulated optional demographic fields.
outputs.priority_justification: Including blank values makes results more complete across several reporting contexts, although other system functions do not depend on this behavior.

outputs.name: Inactive Patron Reports
outputs.description: The system must generate lists of patrons with no circulation or electronic activity during a configurable number of days. Electronic activity includes account or OPAC logins, online holds, online renewals, and logged access to integrated digital collections. Users must be able to select System, Home Library, County, or another required organizational level; include current mailing addresses; separately identify patrons with outstanding fines; exclude specified categories such as do-not-disturb, VIP, staff, or opted-out patrons; and export results to CSV. The report must support background processing and retrieval of completed results.
outputs.priority_justification: Inactive-patron lists can support outreach and account review, but they are a specialized report with substantial optional criteria.

outputs.name: Anonymized Demographic Statistics
outputs.description: The system must produce demographic statistics, including transactions by geographic region and age range, using anonymized data that does not identify individual patrons.
outputs.priority_justification: Anonymized demographic statistics support planning while protecting patron identity, but they are one analytical use of the reporting system.

outputs.name: Bibliographic Report Catalogue
outputs.description: The system must report bibliographic-record counts, edited-record counts, records added by user and library, records without attached volumes, and records missing specified MARC fields.
outputs.priority_justification: Bibliographic reports help staff monitor record quality and catalog activity, but they are one part of the broader report catalogue.

outputs.name: Bills Report Catalogue
outputs.description: The system must provide reports for bills currently owed by patrons, detailed payments received, detailed forgive/work/goods payments, detailed voids, and aged debt.
outputs.priority_justification: Bills reports support account and debt review, but they are a specialized set of outputs within the reporting platform.

outputs.name: Cancel Report Execution
outputs.description: Users must be able to cancel a report that is scheduled or currently running.
outputs.priority_justification: Cancellation helps users recover from unwanted or resource-intensive report runs, but it is a control around execution rather than a reporting prerequisite.

outputs.name: Canned Report Interface
outputs.description: The system must provide generic canned reports that users can run immediately or schedule to run ASAP, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly. Users must be able to select multiple reports to run together and view their results in one document.
outputs.priority_justification: Canned and scheduled reports reduce repeated work, but users can still produce results through other report interfaces.

outputs.name: Circulation Report Catalogue
outputs.description: The system must provide circulation reports for check-in and checkout counts; overdue items with relevant contact information; circulation by modifier, category, Dewey classification, shelving location, MARC fields, patron county, home library, and age; renewals; non-cataloged circulation; and total circulation, including combined cataloged and non-cataloged counts.
outputs.priority_justification: The circulation catalogue covers many useful operational questions, but no single listed report is identified as a gating requirement.

outputs.name: Collection Value Reports
outputs.description: The system must report item values based on item-record data for the entire collection or a selected portion, including items selected by status, format, collection, call number, or shelving location.
outputs.priority_justification: Collection value reports can inform budgeting and collection review, though the system can provide its main operational reporting without valuations.

outputs.name: Count Check-In Types
outputs.description: The system must count check-ins individually and cumulatively by method, including book drop, terminal, staff user, and self-service. Check-in date and time reporting must distinguish check-ins from renewals.
outputs.priority_justification: Separating check-in methods and renewals makes circulation statistics more informative, though broader reporting can operate without that detail.

outputs.name: Count Check-Out Types
outputs.description: The system must count checkouts individually and cumulatively by staff checkout, self-checkout, staff renewal, self-checkout renewal, online renewal, and OPAC renewal.
outputs.priority_justification: Distinguishing checkout and renewal methods helps analyze service usage, but it is a detailed breakdown rather than a core system dependency.

outputs.name: Data Quality Reports
outputs.description: The system must provide reports identifying data-quality problems, including items with invalid item types or excessively long call numbers and bibliographic records without item records.
outputs.priority_justification: Data-quality reports help staff find invalid or incomplete records across several sources, but they support maintenance rather than core report execution.

outputs.name: Display Report Criteria
outputs.description: The system must display the query selections and clearly defined selection criteria with report results. Results must also identify the report name and selected date criteria.
outputs.priority_justification: Showing criteria with results improves interpretability and reproducibility, though reports can still run without this presentation feature.

outputs.name: Error Reporting and Feedback
outputs.description: The system must provide high-level error reporting and feedback and low-level query-specific feedback through the front-end interface for Local and Global System Administrators.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 marks administrator error feedback Medium Priority, so it can aid troubleshooting without being necessary for report execution.
outputs.source_priority_note: D10 marks this Medium Priority

outputs.name: Executive Board Reports
outputs.description: The system must provide predefined reports for library boards and other external consumers, including basic statistics required by the Georgia Annual Report and Application for State Aid. Activity reports must include checkouts, check-ins, holds placed, and holds filled, with cross-tabulation by terminal, branch, system, hour, patron age range, patron type, and patron location.
outputs.priority_justification: Predefined board and state-aid reports simplify recurring external reporting, but the system can provide other management reports without them.

outputs.name: Financial Reports
outputs.description: The system must report patron account balances by patron, home library, and system; fines and charges by time period and charge type; fines waived by time period and branch; and payments by time period, payment method, and collecting library.
outputs.priority_justification: Financial summaries help staff review balances, fines, waivers, and payments, though they are not required for the system's broader report workflows.

outputs.name: Group Transaction Reports
outputs.description: The system must group transactions by hour, terminal, branch, and system and support queries for all transactions or transaction types, including check-ins, checkouts, fines collected, and patron registrations.
outputs.priority_justification: Grouping transactions by time and location helps managers analyze activity, but it is one of several useful report dimensions.

outputs.name: Historical Reporting
outputs.description: The system must support reporting on data as it existed at a specified prior date or date range, including historical shelving locations and snapshots of bills. This reporting capability does not prescribe a particular storage architecture.
outputs.priority_justification: Historical snapshots support comparisons and audits across several sources, but the system can deliver current reporting without this capability.

outputs.name: Hold Report Catalogue
outputs.description: The system must provide reports for hold purchase alerts, items sent or received for holds, IntraPINES loans by system or facility, unfilled holds, annual hold counts, and stale holds awaiting pickup.
outputs.priority_justification: Hold reports help staff monitor fulfillment and stale requests, but the broader system can run without this particular report catalogue.

outputs.name: Item Report Catalogue
outputs.description: The system must provide item reports for items added, deleted, edited, counted, currently checked out, overdue, long overdue, missing, in transit, claimed returned, or created within a date range; items selected by use count or fines-stopped reason; weeding information; last copies deleted; and collection age or value by call number or shelving location.
outputs.priority_justification: The item report catalogue supports collection management and troubleshooting, while other reporting functions can operate independently.

outputs.name: Item Usage Reports
outputs.description: The system must report total item-use counts and counts for selected date ranges, including fiscal-year and monthly use, and provide last-circulation dates and weeding data such as date of last circulation and circulation count.
outputs.priority_justification: Item-use and last-circulation data support collection and weeding decisions, but these analyses are not required for other reporting workflows.

outputs.name: Manage Patron Financial Data
outputs.description: The system must associate fines, charges, waivers, and ecommerce transactions with patron and item records; support financial queries joining those records; allow financial information to be updated and reflected promptly; track fines waived and payments by library; and allow users to query accounts above a specified balance.
outputs.priority_justification: Associating financial activity with patrons and items supports account review and reconciliation, but this functionality is a specialized reporting domain.

outputs.name: Manage Report Templates
outputs.description: Administrators must be able to create report templates available to staff. Staff must be able to run templates as-is or modify only permitted selections, with changes preserving dependable results. Authorized users must also be able to create templates for PINES libraries and clone an existing template into a separate variant.
outputs.priority_justification: Templates let staff reuse dependable reports across multiple libraries, but ad hoc reporting can function without template management.

outputs.name: On-Demand Report Interface
outputs.description: The system must provide an on-demand reporting interface for preset maintenance, collection-development, and similar reports, allowing users to edit selection criteria and display options before execution.
outputs.priority_justification: Editing criteria before execution gives users control over preset reports, though other reporting modes can cover the same general need.

outputs.name: Open Template Reporting
outputs.description: The system must provide open-template reporting with circulation, item, patron, bill, and bibliographic attributes available for filtering and display.
outputs.priority_justification: Open-template reporting makes common data attributes available for flexible analysis, but it is one interface option among several.

outputs.name: Patron Report Catalogue
outputs.description: The system must provide reports for patron counts and additions; patrons by demographic category, age, county, city, ZIP code, home library, profile group, survey response, expiration date, inactive or barred status, and note wording; voter survey responses; and staff accounts by password-change date and account expiration.
outputs.priority_justification: Patron reports support account and demographic analysis, but the wide list represents useful reporting coverage rather than a standalone system prerequisite.

outputs.name: Periodic Management Reports
outputs.description: The system must provide periodic management reports for bibliographic records with holds; items not checked out for a specified number of days; item-level holds; invalid item types; in-transit items with outstanding holds; last copies; long call numbers; missing items; bibliographic records without item records; and patrons with invalid home libraries.
outputs.priority_justification: These periodic reports cover useful catalog and patron maintenance checks, but they are a collection of scheduled analyses rather than a system prerequisite.

outputs.name: Prioritize Report Queue
outputs.description: The system must allow designated report types, such as board reports, to be prioritized ahead of lower-priority or resource-consuming reports in the execution queue.
outputs.priority_justification: Queue prioritization can get time-sensitive board reports ahead of resource-intensive jobs, though the sources' emphasis does not make it a core requirement.
outputs.source_priority_note: D12 describes report prioritization as crucial and states that important reports should be able to jump the queue

outputs.name: Process Description Documentation
outputs.description: Product documentation must provide high-level descriptions of major processes, including bibliographic record import and export, validation against internal and external authority sources, and standard reports.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 marks high-level process documentation Medium Priority, making it useful for understanding workflows but less urgent than operating capabilities.
outputs.source_priority_note: D10 marks this Medium Priority

outputs.name: Real-Time Reporting
outputs.description: The system must support reports using current data in real time, including reports used to monitor current activity.
outputs.priority_justification: Current-data reports help monitor live activity, but not every management report requires real-time results.

outputs.name: Report Output Formats
outputs.description: The system must provide reports in Excel, HTML, CSV, and pivot-table formats.
outputs.priority_justification: Multiple output formats make results easier to analyze and share, but the reporting system can operate with a narrower set of formats.

outputs.name: Report Queue Visibility
outputs.description: Staff must be able to view their report's queue position, the number of reports ahead, submission time, and status, including waiting, running, completed, or failed.
outputs.priority_justification: Queue status helps staff understand report progress across several sources, but it does not determine whether reports can execute.

outputs.name: Separate System Environments
outputs.description: The system must provide separate development, training, and production environments. The training environment must allow staff to practice without risking production data, and configurations such as templates, permissions, and saved queries must be migratable into production.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 marks development and training environments with configuration migration Medium Priority; staff benefit from safe practice, but production reporting can run without them.
outputs.source_priority_note: D10 marks development and training environments with configuration migration Medium Priority

outputs.name: Single-Row MARC Reporting
outputs.description: The system must extract selected MARC fields for reports and display those fields on a single row of report data, including when the fields are stored across multiple rows.
outputs.priority_justification: Single-row MARC extraction makes selected bibliographic fields easier to use in reports, but it is a specialized data presentation need.

outputs.name: Staff Login Methods
outputs.description: The system must support individual staff authentication using traditional username and password and an optional streamlined method such as an employee-card swipe. Card-based login must not be required or bypass individual authentication, and the system must identify which staff member is logged in.
outputs.priority_justification: Individual authentication and staff identification support accountable access, while the optional card method remains a convenience.

outputs.name: Supported Web Browsers
outputs.description: When accessed through a web browser, the system must support Microsoft Internet Explorer version 6.0 or later and Mozilla Firefox version 2.0 or later.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 explicitly marks the legacy browser support requirement Medium Priority, so it is valuable for compatibility but not a top-tier system condition.
outputs.source_priority_note: D10 marks this Medium Priority

outputs.name: Transaction History Retention
outputs.description: The system must retain detailed transaction history for a configurable number of days and retain monthly and annual aggregate information indefinitely.
outputs.priority_justification: Retaining detailed and aggregate transactions supports historical analysis, but the requested retention policy is not identified as a legal obligation here.

outputs.name: Transaction Summary Reports
outputs.description: The system must report holds placed, holds filled, and checkouts per patron, library, selected group of libraries, system, or county. Reports must display checkout and placed-hold counts per patron and subtotal holds by type, including active, frozen, and frozen-until holds.
outputs.priority_justification: These summaries help compare hold and checkout activity across organizational scopes, but they are one analytical report family.

outputs.name: Uncataloged Material Inventory
outputs.description: The system must track uncataloged materials, including paperback books and children's board books, as inventory before individual catalog records are complete. It must support rapid distribution with minimal branch labor, identify material use, and include related transactions in circulation statistics and reports.
outputs.priority_justification: Tracking uncataloged materials supports rapid distribution and more complete circulation statistics, though it concerns a specific collection workflow.

outputs.name: Workstation Transaction Reports
outputs.description: The system must report transactions by specified date and time, workstation, or staff member to support analysis of activity and staff workflow.
outputs.priority_justification: Workstation- and staff-level transaction reports help analyze activity and workflow, though the system can provide general transaction reporting without them.

outputs.name: Configuration Migration
outputs.description: The system must provide export and import functionality to migrate configurations developed in development or training into production, including report templates, permission settings, and other configuration.
outputs.priority_justification: Migrating templates and permissions reduces configuration rework between environments, though the system can report without this deployment convenience.

outputs.name: Vendor Data Integration
outputs.description: The system must support data exchange with vendor websites through published APIs or automated transfers of standard-format data files, including USMARC21 and EDIFACT, while accommodating locations where particular vendor data is unavailable.
outputs.priority_justification: Vendor data exchange supports purchasing and processing workflows, but the request is limited to two sources and allows locations without particular vendor data.

outputs.name: Prevent Duplicate Export Rows
outputs.description: Report exports must avoid unintended duplicate rows so exported data can be used without repeated records.
outputs.priority_justification: Preventing unintended duplicate export rows improves the usability of exported data, though the single-source feature does not block other report functions.

outputs.name: Alert Transfer Problems
outputs.description: The system must notify responsible staff when an item transfer is delayed or encounters an issue.
outputs.priority_justification: Problem alerts can help staff respond sooner, but delayed-transfer notification is a single-source convenience rather than a prerequisite for tracking transfers.

outputs.name: Print Transit Labels
outputs.description: The system must generate printable transit labels containing barcodes for items being transferred.
outputs.priority_justification: Barcode transit labels can simplify physical handling, but staff can move items without this single-source printing feature.

outputs.name: Share Transfer Queries
outputs.description: The system must allow authorized users to share saved transfer queries with other authorized users.
outputs.priority_justification: Sharing queries is a convenience for teams, but the single-source request does not make it necessary for users to run their own transfer queries.

outputs.name: Undo Completed Transfers
outputs.description: The system must allow an authorized user to undo an item transfer when an incorrect transfer has been completed.
outputs.priority_justification: Undoing a completed transfer is a useful recovery option, but it is a single-source safeguard rather than a core reporting capability.

outputs.name: Review Purge Candidates
outputs.description: The system must provide read-only reports of item records identified as purge candidates so users can review them without changing or deleting records through the reports.
outputs.priority_justification: Read-only candidate reports provide a convenient review step, but the request appears in only D06 and is not required to identify candidates.

outputs.name: Report Deletion Activity
outputs.description: The system must report deletion activity for a selected period, including totals and breakdowns by record type, location, system, and user, and identify users with the highest deletion counts.
outputs.priority_justification: Deletion activity summaries help administrators review patterns, but the single-source request is an additional analysis rather than a core workflow.

outputs.name: Track Denied Deletions
outputs.description: The system must track deletion attempts that are denied so administrators can identify attempted deletions of records that users should not delete.
outputs.priority_justification: Tracking denied attempts can help administrators investigate unusual behavior, but it is requested only in D07 and does not block ordinary deletion auditing.

outputs.name: Configure Patron Age Ranges
outputs.description: The system must allow age ranges used for patron filtering and grouping to be configured for each report and calculated from patrons' birth dates. Configurations must support user-defined brackets such as 0–5, 6–10, and 11–15.
outputs.priority_justification: Configurable age brackets add flexibility for particular analyses, but users can run patron reports without custom ranges.

outputs.name: Comparative Report Columns
outputs.description: The system must support report outputs with comparative columns for periods such as last month's circulation, the previous month's circulation, percentage difference, the corresponding month of the previous year, and percentage difference between those periods.
outputs.priority_justification: Comparative period columns can make trends easier to interpret, but this is a specialized output enhancement.

outputs.name: Edit Canned Report Displays
outputs.description: Authorized users must be able to add canned reports according to their permissions and edit canned-report display fields, such as adding shelving location.
outputs.priority_justification: Editing canned-report display fields gives authorized users flexibility, but the core reports can remain useful with fixed displays.

outputs.name: Edit Recurring Reports
outputs.description: Users must be able to edit recurring reports by adding or removing report selections and changing the report's email recipients.
outputs.priority_justification: Editing recurring selections and recipients helps maintain scheduled reports, but this single-source refinement is not required to run them.

outputs.name: Email Report Delivery
outputs.description: The system must allow users to deliver reports by email, enter recipients, and select recipients from an address book of regularly used addresses.
outputs.priority_justification: Email delivery and saved recipients add convenience, but users can retrieve and share reports through other means.

outputs.name: Filter Surveys By Name
outputs.description: Users must be able to select a survey by its name rather than entering its identifier, and the system must resolve the name to the corresponding survey record.
outputs.priority_justification: Selecting surveys by name is a usability improvement for a narrow report filter, and users can otherwise enter the identifier.

outputs.name: In-House Use Reports
outputs.description: The system must report non-cataloged in-house use counts by month and cataloged in-house use counts.
outputs.priority_justification: In-house use counts add a limited view of material use, but the request appears only in D10 and other circulation reports remain available.

outputs.name: Notice Activity Reports
outputs.description: The system must support reports on pre-overdue notices, overdue notices, and holds notices sent.
outputs.priority_justification: Notice activity reports provide a useful service snapshot, but this limited report family is only specified in D10.

outputs.name: Patron Behavior Statistics
outputs.description: The system must produce statistics for understanding and predicting patron behavior and material use, including average return speed for a particular book, likelihood of renewal, renewal rates, and the percentage of branch checkouts that are renewals.
outputs.priority_justification: Predictive behavior measures can inform planning, but the specialized statistics are requested by only two sources and are not core operations.

outputs.name: Report Hold Placement Methods
outputs.description: The system must count hold requests and report how each hold was placed, including at a staff desk, at a public computer inside the library, or remotely.
outputs.priority_justification: Hold-placement channels offer a useful service-use breakdown, but the single-source detail is not necessary for hold reporting generally.

outputs.name: Upload Report Filters
outputs.description: Users must be able to upload a text file containing values such as barcodes or TCNs and use those values to filter a report.
outputs.priority_justification: Uploading barcode or TCN filters can save time for selected tasks, but users can filter reports through other query methods.

outputs.name: Configuration Migration
outputs.description: The reporting system must support migration of configuration between environments.
outputs.priority_justification: Configuration migration is useful for moving reporting setups between environments, but this brief single-source request provides little detail about scope.

outputs.name: Detailed Aged Debt Report
outputs.description: The system must provide an aged-debt report with detailed debt information.
outputs.priority_justification: Detailed aged-debt reporting adds useful financial detail, but it is requested by only D14 and is not required for general financial reports.

outputs.name: Item Edit Date Reporting
outputs.description: Item reports must show the last edit date based on item edits only; circulation activity must not change or be included in that date.
outputs.priority_justification: Separating item edits from circulation activity makes one report field more precise, but it is a narrow refinement requested by two sources.

messages.content:
You are the reviewer of a requirements document. The user message is JSON with the current requirements (with ids R01...), the glossary, the blacklist of discarded requirements (context only), the review round and the maximum number of rounds.

Validate the list itself; you do not have the corpus, so do not ask for new requirements. Flag defects only, things a careful reader would call wrong, not things that are merely imperfect. Each issue lists the involved requirement ids and explains the problem concretely. Issue types:
- duplicate: two or more requirements that ask for the same capability (not one that duplicates a blacklisted item).
- conflict: two requirements that cannot both be satisfied by one system (logically incompatible). A rule interacting with another feature (for example a null-inclusion rule and a filter) is not a conflict; when in doubt, raise wording.
- wording: vocabulary inconsistent with the glossary, or a name that does not match its description.
- nonsense: an item that is not a software requirement or makes no sense.
- too_broad: one issue per requirement that clearly bundles several independently testable capabilities per the definition below. Length alone is not a reason, and a description that lists several options, filters or fields of one capability is not too_broad.
- too_narrow: a requirement that is only a detail of another (one filter option, one field, one exclusion rule of a report or utility). requirement_ids contain both the detail and its parent, and the explanation says which is which.
- priority: a priority that is implausible under the scale below or clashes with its own justification.
- High: Core to the system's purpose or requested by many stakeholders; the system is not acceptable without it.
- Medium: Clearly valuable and requested, but the system can go live without it and add it in a later release.
- Low: Nice to have, requested by a single stakeholder or marginal to the core workflows; implement only if time allows.

Requirements tagged "[granularity settled]" next to their id were already split or folded by a resolver: raise no too_broad or too_narrow on them (the other issue types still apply).

Route:
- accept: the list is clean, the remaining concerns are matters of taste, or they are only granularity concerns on "[granularity settled]" requirements.
- targeted: there are defects worth fixing.

Definition of a requirement: A requirement describes one capability, rule or quality the system must provide, at the level a tester would write one acceptance test for. It names what, for whom, and under what condition, and it is independent of how it is implemented. Two statements are the same requirement if a tester would write one test for both. A statement is too broad if its acceptance test would have to be several unrelated tests. A statement is too narrow if it only makes sense as a detail of another requirement, such as one filter option of a report.

Example of a statement that is too broad: "Staff can manage item transfers between branches, including selecting candidate items by circulation history and keeping an audit history of every completed transfer." This is exactly two requirements: (1) select transfer candidates by circulation history, (2) record an audit history of completed transfers.
Example of statements that are too narrow: "The inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch" and "The inactive patron report can be filtered by patron profile". These are one requirement: the inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch and patron profile.

   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "A multi-record query builder provides a broad way to create reports across core library data, requested in three sources and central to the reporting platform."
  },
  {
   "id": "R008",
   "name": "Non-Disruptive Report Processing",
   "description": "The system must process searches and reports during open hours without disrupting other system functions, including circulation and patron access to the OPAC. Long-running reports must be capable of background processing or other isolation from operational activity.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D16",
    "D18"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D10 marks open-hours report processing High Priority, and D14, D16, and D18 also address avoiding disruption to live services."
  },
  {
   "id": "R009",
   "name": "Online System Help",
   "description": "The system must provide online HTML help that is hierarchical, cross-linked, and describes and illustrates system functions. Staff must be able to find help without leaving the system, and the help must be accessible to screen-reader users.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D16",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D10 marks online system help High Priority, and the requirement is repeated across five sources, including accessibility for screen-reader users."
  },
  {
   "id": "R010",
   "name": "Payment Audit Ledger",
   "description": "The system must maintain a ledger of patron payments identifying the specific charges to which each payment was applied, so finance staff can trace payments and reconcile accounts.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D11",
    "D17"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D11 calls the financial audit trail critical, and finance staff need payment-to-charge detail to trace and reconcile accounts."
  },
  {
   "id": "R011",
   "name": "Preserve OPAC Functionality",
   "description": "Management reporting functionality must not constrain or adversely affect the functionality or performance of the Online Public Access Catalog.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D16",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D10 marks OPAC preservation High Priority, and D16 calls separation from OPAC functionality critical because reporting must not impair patron access."
  },
  {
   "id": "R012",
   "name": "Privacy-Protecting Transaction Archives",
   "description": "The system must archive transaction data for the period required by applicable law while protecting patron privacy by removing personally identifiable information and retaining useful demographic statistics.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D12"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D12 states that State law requires transaction retention and privacy protection, making the archive behavior a compliance obligation."
  },
  {
   "id": "R013",
   "name": "Record Data Specifications",
   "description": "Product documentation must provide complete data specifications for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold/request, and other records maintained or accessed by the Management Processes, including field names, data types, and relationships.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D10 marks complete record data specifications High Priority, and these details support administration and interpretation across the system's record types."
  },
  {
   "id": "R014",
   "name": "Relational Database Support",
   "description": "The system must use and work with a fully relational database structure and support reporting queries across relational data. It must not require a denormalized reporting schema synchronized with the live database.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D16",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D10 marks relational database support High Priority, and the requirement is repeated across four sources for reporting against relational data."
  },
  {
   "id": "R015",
   "name": "Role-Based Access Control",
   "description": "The system must control user rights through security groups or roles assigned to individuals, workgroups, and staff groups, and allow administrators to manage permissions through role assignment. Roles must support access appropriate to staff, managers, local administrators, and global administrators.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D13",
    "D16",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D10 marks role-based access High Priority, and the requirement is repeated in several sources for controlling staff and administrator permissions."
  },
  {
   "id": "R016",
   "name": "Server Operating Environment",
   "description": "The system must operate on Linux or Solaris servers, including the Linux and Solaris environments used for production and disaster recovery.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D16",
    "D18"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D10 marks Linux or Solaris operation High Priority, and D16 and D18 also specify those server environments."
  },
  {
   "id": "R017",
   "name": "Standards-Compliant HTML",
   "description": "The system must produce standards-compliant HTML for web interfaces, help content, and report output.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D16",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D10 marks standards-compliant HTML High Priority, with three other sources also specifying the output requirement."
  },
  {
   "id": "R018",
   "name": "Transit Location Reports",
   "description": "The system must report items in transit by sending library and destination library, and provide reports of items currently in transit between locations for delivery coordination.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D18"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D18 explicitly records in-transit item reports as critical, and delivery coordination depends on knowing sending and destination locations."
  },
  {
   "id": "R019",
   "name": "Enforce Archive Retention",
   "description": "The system must enforce data-archiving retention policies required for audits, including a seven-year retention period where applicable under state and local requirements.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D11",
    "D12"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "The requirement specifies retention periods required for audits, including seven years where state and local rules apply, making enforcement a compliance obligation."
  },
  {
   "id": "R020",
   "name": "Read-Only OPAC Data Access",
   "description": "Management Processes must interact with the OPAC patron interface by querying data such as holds and circulation transactions, without modifying that data.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D19"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "Read-only OPAC access protects patron-facing holds and circulation data from management-process changes, aligning with the multi-source requirement to preserve OPAC functionality."
  },
  {
   "id": "R021",
   "name": "Material Volume Reporting",
   "description": "The system must report material volume for a specified library at the current time or a selected historical point, separating new acquisitions, items on the shelf, items in circulation, and totals. Users must be able to break results down by categories such as total items, holds, adult fiction, and board books, customize categories, and report volume added in periods such as the last 30, 60, or 90 days.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D01",
    "D10",
    "D15"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "The reports support collection planning, but the system can provide its broader reporting workflows without every requested volume breakdown."
  },
  {
   "id": "R022",
   "name": "Branch Capacity Interface",
   "description": "The system must provide authorized users, including branch managers, an overview of capacity across all branches, with the ability to drill into individual branches, sort and filter by region, library type, and current load, view growth or shrinkage trends, and export the information to CSV. The capacity measure itself remains to be defined.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D02",
    "D10",
    "D17"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Branch managers gain useful capacity and trend visibility, though the capacity measure is still undefined and other management reporting can operate without it."
  },
  {
   "id": "R023",
   "name": "Shelf Space Usage Report",
   "description": "The system must compare, for each material genre and format, the percentage of total circulations, the percentage of the collection, and the percentage of total shelf space. Results must be available per library and system-wide, support date-range comparisons, and provide a side-by-side library comparison view. When shelf-space measurements are unavailable, the system must estimate shelf space using available item dimensions or item count as a proxy.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D03",
    "D10",
    "D15",
    "D18"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "The comparisons help libraries make collection and shelf-space decisions, but they are a specialized analysis rather than a prerequisite for core reporting."
  },
  {
   "id": "R024",
   "name": "Generate Transfer Pull Lists",
   "description": "The system must generate printable pull lists identifying items selected for transfer so staff can retrieve them for movement.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D04",
    "D10"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Printable pull lists help staff retrieve selected items accurately, while transfers can still be coordinated through other procedures."
  },
  {
   "id": "R025",
   "name": "Preview Pending Transfers",
   "description": "Before applying a transfer, the system must show a preview of the proposed changes, including the number of items and their source and destination locations, and require confirmation before making the changes.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D04"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "A preview and confirmation reduce accidental transfer changes, but they support rather than enable the system's broader workflows."
  },
  {
   "id": "R026",
   "name": "Query Transfer Candidates",
   "description": "The system must allow authorized staff to query for candidate materials for transfer or other administrative processing, using conditions such as material type, section, genre, or circulation history.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D04",
    "D15",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Candidate queries help staff identify materials for transfer and administrative work, but are one workflow within the broader system."
  },
  {
   "id": "R027",
   "name": "Restrict Transfer Permissions",
   "description": "The system must restrict item transfers to authorized roles, including managers, administrators, or transfer coordinators, and prevent unauthorized staff from performing transfers.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D04"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Role restrictions reduce the risk of unauthorized transfers, although this control applies to a narrower workflow than the system's general access management."
  },
  {
   "id": "R028",
   "name": "Revert Transferred Items",
   "description": "The system must automatically or manually return transferred items to their original locations after a configured period or when configured criteria are met. Supported criteria include time-based conditions and item-status or destination events; the sources do not establish whether checkout at the destination should trigger reversion.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D04",
    "D10",
    "D15",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Automatic or criteria-based reversion can reduce manual work for temporary transfers, though the sources leave some trigger behavior unresolved."
  },
  {
   "id": "R029",
   "name": "Save Reusable Queries",
   "description": "The system must allow users to save queries for repeated use, including recurring transfer and reporting tasks.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D04",
    "D15",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Reusable queries reduce repeated setup for recurring tasks, although users can still run those tasks by recreating queries."
  },
  {
   "id": "R030",
   "name": "Select Transfer Results",
   "description": "The system must allow staff to manually select individual titles or items from query results, including selecting only part of a larger candidate set for subsequent administrative processing.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D04",
    "D15",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Selecting only relevant query results gives staff control over transfer batches, though the overall system can function without this refinement."
  },
  {
   "id": "R031",
   "name": "Transfer History Records",
   "description": "The system must retain transfer activity for audit and expose item transfer history so staff can review completed and reverted transfers and determine how often an item has moved.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D04"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Transfer history helps staff audit movements and answer item-history questions, but it is specific to the transfer utility."
  },
  {
   "id": "R032",
   "name": "Transfer Item Batches",
   "description": "The system must provide a utility for transferring batches of items between branches or other locations, including mobile libraries, outreach collections, warehouses, book sales, and event locations.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D04",
    "D10",
    "D15"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Batch transfers streamline moving materials across locations, while the wider management system can operate without this utility."
  },
  {
   "id": "R033",
   "name": "Update Item Locations",
   "description": "The system must allow authorized staff to change the location records of selected items to the transfer destination.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D04",
    "D15",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Updating locations completes the transfer workflow, but transfers are one operational utility among the system's broader reporting functions."
  },
  {
   "id": "R034",
   "name": "Delayed Transit Items Report",
   "description": "The system must generate one report of items that have remained in transit longer than a configurable number of days, with views per branch and system-wide. The report must combine transit-to and transit-from items, identify items with no arrival date and an overdue departure date, and allow sorting by due date. Seven days is suggested as the default threshold.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D05",
    "D10",
    "D15",
    "D18"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "The report helps staff investigate overdue transit items, while the broader system can operate without this particular exception report."
  },
  {
   "id": "R035",
   "name": "Missing Damaged Items Report",
   "description": "The system must provide a report of missing and damaged items by branch. The report must include item condition notes and support date ranges for trend analysis.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D05",
    "D10",
    "D15",
    "D18"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Branch-level missing and damaged-item trends inform collection oversight, but this specialized report is not needed for other reporting workflows."
  },
  {
   "id": "R036",
   "name": "Audit Record Deletions",
   "description": "The system must retain an audit record of successful deletions, including record type, record identifier, timestamp, user, and user location. This tracking must cover purge activity and other record deletions.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D06",
    "D07",
    "D10",
    "D15"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Deletion audit records help administrators investigate changes across several source documents, but the system's reporting workflows can run without the audit feature."
  },
  {
   "id": "R037",
   "name": "Batch Status Conversion",
   "description": "The system must support converting multiple items from one status to another in a batch, such as changing items from missing to discard/weed, and provide a report or workflow to assist with the conversion.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D06",
    "D10",
    "D15"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Batch status conversion can reduce repetitive cleanup work, though staff can change statuses through other workflows."
  },
  {
   "id": "R038",
   "name": "Confirm Purge Deletions",
   "description": "The system must require a separate confirmation step before executing purge deletions, distinct from identifying and reviewing candidates.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D06"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "A separate confirmation step helps prevent accidental purge deletions, but it supports rather than enables candidate identification and review."
  },
  {
   "id": "R039",
   "name": "Delete Itemless Records",
   "description": "The system must provide a method to delete records that have no items attached during collection cleanup.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D06",
    "D10",
    "D15"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Removing itemless records helps keep the catalog clean, although users can operate the reporting system without this cleanup method."
  },
  {
   "id": "R040",
   "name": "Delete Volumes With Copies",
   "description": "The system must provide a method to delete volume entries together with their associated copy entries during collection cleanup.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D06",
    "D10",
    "D15"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Deleting volumes with associated copies supports collection cleanup, but it is a specialized maintenance operation rather than a general reporting dependency."
  },
  {
   "id": "R041",
   "name": "Identify Purge Candidates",
   "description": "The system must identify item records eligible for purging using customizable, combinable criteria, including status (such as missing, discard/weed, or damaged), time spent in a status, and time since last circulation.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D06",
    "D10",
    "D15"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Customizable purge criteria help staff identify records for collection cleanup, but review and deletion workflows can be delivered separately."
  },
  {
   "id": "R042",
   "name": "Filter Patron Reports",
   "description": "The system must allow patron queries and reports to be limited by age range, ZIP code, county of residence, home branch, patron type, and preferred language. Users must be able to combine these filters with other conditions using AND and OR logic.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D08",
    "D10"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "These filters support patron-focused program planning, but the reports remain useful without every demographic and geographic selection."
  },
  {
   "id": "R043",
   "name": "Group Patron Reports",
   "description": "The system must group patron queries and reports by age range, ZIP code, county of residence, home branch, patron type, and preferred language, and show aggregates such as circulation counts and patron counts for each group.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D08",
    "D10"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Grouping patron results helps organizations compare program reach, though it is a specialized analysis rather than a prerequisite for reporting."
  },
  {
   "id": "R044",
   "name": "Include Null Report Values",
   "description": "Report results must include records with null or blank values rather than silently excluding them, including patrons with unpopulated optional demographic fields.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D08",
    "D10",
    "D19",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Including blank values makes results more complete across several reporting contexts, although other system functions do not depend on this behavior."
  },
  {
   "id": "R045",
   "name": "Inactive Patron Reports",
   "description": "The system must generate lists of patrons with no circulation or electronic activity during a configurable number of days. Electronic activity includes account or OPAC logins, online holds, online renewals, and logged access to integrated digital collections. Users must be able to select System, Home Library, County, or another required organizational level; include current mailing addresses; separately identify patrons with outstanding fines; exclude specified categories such as do-not-disturb, VIP, staff, or opted-out patrons; and export results to CSV. The report must support background processing and retrieval of completed results.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D09",
    "D10"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Inactive-patron lists can support outreach and account review, but they are a specialized report with substantial optional criteria."
  },
  {
   "id": "R046",
   "name": "Anonymized Demographic Statistics",
   "description": "The system must produce demographic statistics, including transactions by geographic region and age range, using anonymized data that does not identify individual patrons.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D17",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Anonymized demographic statistics support planning while protecting patron identity, but they are one analytical use of the reporting system."
  },
  {
   "id": "R047",
   "name": "Bibliographic Report Catalogue",
   "description": "The system must report bibliographic-record counts, edited-record counts, records added by user and library, records without attached volumes, and records missing specified MARC fields.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Bibliographic reports help staff monitor record quality and catalog activity, but they are one part of the broader report catalogue."
  },
  {
   "id": "R048",
   "name": "Bills Report Catalogue",
   "description": "The system must provide reports for bills currently owed by patrons, detailed payments received, detailed forgive/work/goods payments, detailed voids, and aged debt.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Bills reports support account and debt review, but they are a specialized set of outputs within the reporting platform."
  },
  {
   "id": "R049",
   "name": "Cancel Report Execution",
   "description": "Users must be able to cancel a report that is scheduled or currently running.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D19",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Cancellation helps users recover from unwanted or resource-intensive report runs, but it is a control around execution rather than a reporting prerequisite."
  },
  {
   "id": "R050",
   "name": "Canned Report Interface",
   "description": "The system must provide generic canned reports that users can run immediately or schedule to run ASAP, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly. Users must be able to select multiple reports to run together and view their results in one document.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Canned and scheduled reports reduce repeated work, but users can still produce results through other report interfaces."
  },
  {
   "id": "R051",
   "name": "Circulation Report Catalogue",
   "description": "The system must provide circulation reports for check-in and checkout counts; overdue items with relevant contact information; circulation by modifier, category, Dewey classification, shelving location, MARC fields, patron county, home library, and age; renewals; non-cataloged circulation; and total circulation, including combined cataloged and non-cataloged counts.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "The circulation catalogue covers many useful operational questions, but no single listed report is identified as a gating requirement."
  },
  {
   "id": "R052",
   "name": "Collection Value Reports",
   "description": "The system must report item values based on item-record data for the entire collection or a selected portion, including items selected by status, format, collection, call number, or shelving location.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D11",
    "D14"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Collection value reports can inform budgeting and collection review, though the system can provide its main operational reporting without valuations."
  },
  {
   "id": "R053",
   "name": "Count Check-In Types",
   "description": "The system must count check-ins individually and cumulatively by method, including book drop, terminal, staff user, and self-service. Check-in date and time reporting must distinguish check-ins from renewals.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Separating check-in methods and renewals makes circulation statistics more informative, though broader reporting can operate without that detail."
  },
  {
   "id": "R054",
   "name": "Count Check-Out Types",
   "description": "The system must count checkouts individually and cumulatively by staff checkout, self-checkout, staff renewal, self-checkout renewal, online renewal, and OPAC renewal.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Distinguishing checkout and renewal methods helps analyze service usage, but it is a detailed breakdown rather than a core system dependency."
  },
  {
   "id": "R055",
   "name": "Data Quality Reports",
   "description": "The system must provide reports identifying data-quality problems, including items with invalid item types or excessively long call numbers and bibliographic records without item records.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D15",
    "D18"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Data-quality reports help staff find invalid or incomplete records across several sources, but they support maintenance rather than core report execution."
  },
  {
   "id": "R056",
   "name": "Display Report Criteria",
   "description": "The system must display the query selections and clearly defined selection criteria with report results. Results must also identify the report name and selected date criteria.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D12",
    "D14"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Showing criteria with results improves interpretability and reproducibility, though reports can still run without this presentation feature."
  },
  {
   "id": "R057",
   "name": "Error Reporting and Feedback",
   "description": "The system must provide high-level error reporting and feedback and low-level query-specific feedback through the front-end interface for Local and Global System Administrators.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "D10 marks administrator error feedback Medium Priority, so it can aid troubleshooting without being necessary for report execution."
  },
  {
   "id": "R058",
   "name": "Executive Board Reports",
   "description": "The system must provide predefined reports for library boards and other external consumers, including basic statistics required by the Georgia Annual Report and Application for State Aid. Activity reports must include checkouts, check-ins, holds placed, and holds filled, with cross-tabulation by terminal, branch, system, hour, patron age range, patron type, and patron location.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D12",
    "D18"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Predefined board and state-aid reports simplify recurring external reporting, but the system can provide other management reports without them."
  },
  {
   "id": "R059",
   "name": "Financial Reports",
   "description": "The system must report patron account balances by patron, home library, and system; fines and charges by time period and charge type; fines waived by time period and branch; and payments by time period, payment method, and collecting library.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D11"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Financial summaries help staff review balances, fines, waivers, and payments, though they are not required for the system's broader report workflows."
  },
  {
