outputs.description: The system must provide read-only reports of item records identified as purge candidates so users can review them without changing or deleting records through the reports.
outputs.priority_justification: Read-only candidate reports provide a convenient review step, but the request appears in only D06 and is not required to identify candidates.

outputs.name: Report Deletion Activity
outputs.description: The system must report deletion activity for a selected period, including totals and breakdowns by record type, location, system, and user, and identify users with the highest deletion counts.
outputs.priority_justification: Deletion activity summaries help administrators review patterns, but the single-source request is an additional analysis rather than a core workflow.

outputs.name: Track Denied Deletions
outputs.description: The system must track deletion attempts that are denied so administrators can identify attempted deletions of records that users should not delete.
outputs.priority_justification: Tracking denied attempts can help administrators investigate unusual behavior, but it is requested only in D07 and does not block ordinary deletion auditing.

outputs.name: Bibliographic Record Counts
outputs.description: The system must report counts of bibliographic records, including records added by each user and library.
outputs.priority_justification: Bibliographic record counts by user and library are a useful management metric, but this specific report appears in only D10 and D14.

outputs.name: Combine Reports Into Documents
outputs.description: The system must allow users to select multiple canned reports to run together and view their results in one document.
outputs.priority_justification: Combining canned reports into one document is a convenience requested in D10, D14, and D20, but separate report results remain usable.

outputs.name: Comparative Report Columns
outputs.description: The system must support report outputs with comparative columns for periods such as last month's circulation, the previous month's circulation, percentage difference, the corresponding month of the previous year, and percentage difference between those periods.
outputs.priority_justification: Comparative period columns can make trends easier to interpret, but this is a specialized output enhancement.

outputs.name: Edited Record Counts
outputs.description: The system must report counts of edited bibliographic records.
outputs.priority_justification: Edited-record counts provide a narrow staff-activity measure requested in D10 and D14, and the system can operate without it.

outputs.name: Email Report Delivery
outputs.description: The system must allow users to deliver reports by email, enter recipients, and select recipients from an address book of regularly used addresses.
outputs.priority_justification: Email delivery and saved recipients add convenience, but users can retrieve and share reports through other means.

outputs.name: Filter Surveys By Name
outputs.description: Users must be able to select a survey by its name rather than entering its identifier, and the system must resolve the name to the corresponding survey record.
outputs.priority_justification: Selecting surveys by name is a usability improvement for a narrow report filter, and users can otherwise enter the identifier.

outputs.name: Forgive Work Goods Report
outputs.description: The system must provide a detailed report of forgive, work, and goods payments.
outputs.priority_justification: This specialized breakdown of forgive, work, and goods payments is requested in D10 and D14 but is narrower than general payment reporting.

outputs.name: Hold Purchase Alert Reports
outputs.description: The system must provide reports identifying hold purchase alerts.
outputs.priority_justification: Hold purchase alert reports are a narrow operational report requested only in D10 and D14.

outputs.name: In-House Use Reports
outputs.description: The system must report non-cataloged in-house use counts by month and cataloged in-house use counts.
outputs.priority_justification: In-house use counts add a limited view of material use, but the request appears only in D10 and other circulation reports remain available.

outputs.name: IntraPINES Loan Reports
outputs.description: The system must provide reports of IntraPINES loans by system or facility.
outputs.priority_justification: IntraPINES loan reports are a specialized reporting need requested in D10 and D14, and are not needed for general reporting workflows.

outputs.name: Notice Activity Reports
outputs.description: The system must support reports on pre-overdue notices, overdue notices, and holds notices sent.
outputs.priority_justification: Notice activity reports provide a useful service snapshot, but this limited report family is only specified in D10.

outputs.name: Patron Behavior Statistics
outputs.description: The system must produce statistics for understanding and predicting patron behavior and material use, including average return speed for a particular book, likelihood of renewal, renewal rates, and the percentage of branch checkouts that are renewals.
outputs.priority_justification: Predictive behavior measures can inform planning, but the specialized statistics are requested by only two sources and are not core operations.

outputs.name: Patron Library Validation Reports
outputs.description: The system must provide periodic management reports identifying patrons with invalid home libraries.
outputs.priority_justification: Invalid-home-library checks are a useful data-cleanup report, but this specific request appears only in D10.

outputs.name: Report Hold Placement Methods
outputs.description: The system must count hold requests and report how each hold was placed, including at a staff desk, at a public computer inside the library, or remotely.
outputs.priority_justification: Hold-placement channels offer a useful service-use breakdown, but the single-source detail is not necessary for hold reporting generally.

outputs.name: Staff Account Reports
outputs.description: The system must provide reports of staff accounts by password-change date and account expiration.
outputs.priority_justification: Staff-account reports on password changes and expiration are a useful administrative check, but the specific reporting need appears only in D10 and D14.

outputs.name: Upload Report Filters
outputs.description: Users must be able to upload a text file containing values such as barcodes or TCNs and use those values to filter a report.
outputs.priority_justification: Uploading barcode or TCN filters can save time for selected tasks, but users can filter reports through other query methods.

outputs.name: Voids Report
outputs.description: The system must provide a detailed report of voids.
outputs.priority_justification: A dedicated voids report is a useful financial review tool, but D10 and D14 request it as a specialized report rather than a core workflow.

outputs.name: Aged Debt Report
outputs.description: The system must provide an aged-debt report with detailed debt information.
outputs.priority_justification: The aged-debt report is requested only in D14 and is a specialized extension of current-bill reporting.

messages.content:
You are the reviewer of a requirements document. The user message is JSON with the current requirements (with ids R01...), the glossary, the blacklist of discarded requirements (context only), the review round and the maximum number of rounds.

Validate the list itself; you do not have the corpus, so do not ask for new requirements. Flag defects only, things a careful reader would call wrong, not things that are merely imperfect. Each issue lists the involved requirement ids and explains the problem concretely. Issue types:
- duplicate: two or more requirements that ask for the same capability (not one that duplicates a blacklisted item).
- conflict: two requirements that cannot both be satisfied by one system (logically incompatible). A rule interacting with another feature (for example a null-inclusion rule and a filter) is not a conflict; when in doubt, raise wording.
- wording: vocabulary inconsistent with the glossary, or a name that does not match its description.
- nonsense: an item that is not a software requirement or makes no sense.
- too_broad: one issue per requirement that clearly bundles several independently testable capabilities per the definition below. Length alone is not a reason, and a description that lists several options, filters or fields of one capability is not too_broad.
- too_narrow: a requirement that is only a detail of another (one filter option, one field, one exclusion rule of a report or utility). requirement_ids contain both the detail and its parent, and the explanation says which is which.
- priority: a priority that is implausible under the scale below or clashes with its own justification.
- High: Core to the system's purpose or requested by many stakeholders; the system is not acceptable without it.
- Medium: Clearly valuable and requested, but the system can go live without it and add it in a later release.
- Low: Nice to have, requested by a single stakeholder or marginal to the core workflows; implement only if time allows.

Requirements tagged "[granularity settled]" next to their id were already split or folded by a resolver: raise no too_broad or too_narrow on them (the other issue types still apply).

Route:
- accept: the list is clean, the remaining concerns are matters of taste, or they are only granularity concerns on "[granularity settled]" requirements.
- targeted: there are defects worth fixing.

Definition of a requirement: A requirement describes one capability, rule or quality the system must provide, at the level a tester would write one acceptance test for. It names what, for whom, and under what condition, and it is independent of how it is implemented. Two statements are the same requirement if a tester would write one test for both. A statement is too broad if its acceptance test would have to be several unrelated tests. A statement is too narrow if it only makes sense as a detail of another requirement, such as one filter option of a report.

Example of a statement that is too broad: "Staff can manage item transfers between branches, including selecting candidate items by circulation history and keeping an audit history of every completed transfer." This is exactly two requirements: (1) select transfer candidates by circulation history, (2) record an audit history of completed transfers.
Example of statements that are too narrow: "The inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch" and "The inactive patron report can be filtered by patron profile". These are one requirement: the inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch and patron profile.

   "priority_justification": "Fine-grained report permissions protect sensitive datasets across multiple sources and complement the system's stated role-based access controls."
  },
  {
   "id": "R003",
   "name": "Assistive Technology Access",
   "description": "The system must support screen readers, screen-magnification software, and other assistive technologies, including JAWS, NVDA, and ZoomText, and comply with Section 508 accessibility requirements.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D16",
    "D18"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D10 marks assistive technology support High Priority, while D16 calls accessibility non-negotiable and D18 describes Section 508 compliance as mandatory."
  },
  {
   "id": "R004",
   "tag": "[granularity settled]",
   "name": "Client Access Platforms and Browsers",
   "description": "The system must be accessible through a web browser or a Windows-compatible client; when accessed through a web browser, it must support Microsoft Internet Explorer version 6.0 or later and Mozilla Firefox version 2.0 or later.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D16",
    "D18"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D10 marks Client Access Platforms as High Priority, making support for the specified client access methods a stated high-priority source requirement."
  },
  {
   "id": "R005",
   "name": "Consortium Scale Support",
   "description": "The system must support a library consortium with 286 locations, 17 million annual circulations, and purchasing or processing more than 900,000 items per year.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D18"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D10 marks consortium-scale support High Priority, and the specified locations, circulation, and processing volumes define the system's operating context."
  },
  {
   "id": "R006",
   "name": "Financial Audit Compliance",
   "description": "The system's reports and archived data must comply with standard accounting practice and applicable state, county, and municipal auditing requirements.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D11"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "The requirement explicitly calls for compliance with applicable state, county, and municipal auditing requirements, so financial reporting must meet those obligations."
  },
  {
   "id": "R007",
   "tag": "[granularity settled]",
   "name": "Item Status Reports",
   "description": "The system must provide periodic management reports identifying items that have not been checked out for a specified number of days, items with item-level holds, in-transit items with outstanding holds, last copies, and missing items.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "The fixed Last Copy Reports requirement depends on identifying last copies, and the requested item-status reports also cover missing and in-transit items used in collection management."
  },
  {
   "id": "R008",
   "tag": "[granularity settled]",
   "name": "Multi-Record Query Interface",
   "description": "The system must provide a user-friendly query-design interface for bibliographic, item, patron, transaction, and financial records. Users must be able to select fields, choose values from picklists, select regular expressions from a dropdown, and use Boolean operators.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D12",
    "D18"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D10, D12, and D18 request querying across major record types, and without a flexible query interface users would be unable to build many of the system’s core reports."
  },
  {
   "id": "R009",
   "name": "Non-Disruptive Report Processing",
   "description": "The system must process searches and reports during open hours without disrupting other system functions, including circulation and patron access to the OPAC. Long-running reports must be capable of background processing or other isolation from operational activity.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D16",
    "D18"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D10 marks open-hours report processing High Priority, and D14, D16, and D18 also address avoiding disruption to live services."
  },
  {
   "id": "R010",
   "name": "Online System Help",
   "description": "The system must provide online HTML help that is hierarchical, cross-linked, and describes and illustrates system functions. Staff must be able to find help without leaving the system, and the help must be accessible to screen-reader users.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D16",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D10 marks online system help High Priority, and the requirement is repeated across five sources, including accessibility for screen-reader users."
  },
  {
   "id": "R011",
   "name": "Payment Audit Ledger",
   "description": "The system must maintain a ledger of patron payments identifying the specific charges to which each payment was applied, so finance staff can trace payments and reconcile accounts.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D11",
    "D17"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D11 calls the financial audit trail critical, and finance staff need payment-to-charge detail to trace and reconcile accounts."
  },
  {
   "id": "R012",
   "name": "Preserve OPAC Functionality",
   "description": "Management reporting functionality must not constrain or adversely affect the functionality or performance of the Online Public Access Catalog.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D16",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D10 marks OPAC preservation High Priority, and D16 calls separation from OPAC functionality critical because reporting must not impair patron access."
  },
  {
   "id": "R013",
   "name": "Privacy-Protecting Transaction Archives",
   "description": "The system must archive transaction data for the period required by applicable law while protecting patron privacy by removing personally identifiable information and retaining useful demographic statistics.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D12"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D12 states that State law requires transaction retention and privacy protection, making the archive behavior a compliance obligation."
  },
  {
   "id": "R014",
   "name": "Record Data Specifications",
   "description": "Product documentation must provide complete data specifications for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold/request, and other records maintained or accessed by the Management Processes, including field names, data types, and relationships.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D10 marks complete record data specifications High Priority, and these details support administration and interpretation across the system's record types."
  },
  {
   "id": "R015",
   "name": "Relational Database Support",
   "description": "The system must use and work with a fully relational database structure and support reporting queries across relational data. It must not require a denormalized reporting schema synchronized with the live database.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D16",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D10 marks relational database support High Priority, and the requirement is repeated across four sources for reporting against relational data."
  },
  {
   "id": "R016",
   "name": "Role-Based Access Control",
   "description": "The system must control user rights through security groups or roles assigned to individuals, workgroups, and staff groups, and allow administrators to manage permissions through role assignment. Roles must support access appropriate to staff, managers, local administrators, and global administrators.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D13",
    "D16",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D10 marks role-based access High Priority, and the requirement is repeated in several sources for controlling staff and administrator permissions."
  },
  {
   "id": "R017",
   "name": "Server Operating Environment",
   "description": "The system must operate on Linux or Solaris servers, including the Linux and Solaris environments used for production and disaster recovery.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D16",
    "D18"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D10 marks Linux or Solaris operation High Priority, and D16 and D18 also specify those server environments."
  },
  {
   "id": "R018",
   "name": "Standards-Compliant HTML",
   "description": "The system must produce standards-compliant HTML for web interfaces, help content, and report output.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D16",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D10 marks standards-compliant HTML High Priority, with three other sources also specifying the output requirement."
  },
  {
   "id": "R019",
   "name": "Transit Location Reports",
   "description": "The system must report items in transit by sending library and destination library, and provide reports of items currently in transit between locations for delivery coordination.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D18"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "D18 explicitly records in-transit item reports as critical, and delivery coordination depends on knowing sending and destination locations."
  },
  {
   "id": "R020",
   "name": "Enforce Archive Retention",
   "description": "The system must enforce data-archiving retention policies required for audits, including a seven-year retention period where applicable under state and local requirements.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D11",
    "D12"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "The requirement specifies retention periods required for audits, including seven years where state and local rules apply, making enforcement a compliance obligation."
  },
  {
   "id": "R021",
   "name": "Read-Only OPAC Data Access",
   "description": "Management Processes must interact with the OPAC patron interface by querying data such as holds and circulation transactions, without modifying that data.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D19"
   ],
   "priority": "High",
   "priority_justification": "Read-only OPAC access protects patron-facing holds and circulation data from management-process changes, aligning with the multi-source requirement to preserve OPAC functionality."
  },
  {
   "id": "R022",
   "name": "Material Volume Reporting",
   "description": "The system must report material volume for a specified library at the current time or a selected historical point, separating new acquisitions, items on the shelf, items in circulation, and totals. Users must be able to break results down by categories such as total items, holds, adult fiction, and board books, customize categories, and report volume added in periods such as the last 30, 60, or 90 days.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D01",
    "D10",
    "D15"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "The reports support collection planning, but the system can provide its broader reporting workflows without every requested volume breakdown."
  },
  {
   "id": "R023",
   "name": "Branch Capacity Interface",
   "description": "The system must provide authorized users, including branch managers, with an overview of capacity across all Branches using a defined capacity measure, with the ability to drill into individual Branches, sort and filter by region, library type, and current load, view growth or shrinkage trends, and export the information to CSV.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D02",
    "D10",
    "D17"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "D02, D10, and D17 support a branch-capacity overview that helps authorized staff compare locations, though reporting can operate without this specialized view."
  },
  {
   "id": "R024",
   "name": "Shelf Space Usage Report",
   "description": "The system must compare, for each material genre and format, the percentage of total circulations, the percentage of the collection, and the percentage of total shelf space. Results must be available per library and system-wide, support date-range comparisons, and provide a side-by-side library comparison view. When shelf-space measurements are unavailable, the system must estimate shelf space using available item dimensions or item count as a proxy.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D03",
    "D10",
    "D15",
    "D18"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "The comparisons help libraries make collection and shelf-space decisions, but they are a specialized analysis rather than a prerequisite for core reporting."
  },
  {
   "id": "R025",
   "name": "Generate Transfer Pull Lists",
   "description": "The system must generate printable pull lists identifying items selected for transfer so staff can retrieve them for movement.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D04",
    "D10"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Printable pull lists help staff retrieve selected items accurately, while transfers can still be coordinated through other procedures."
  },
  {
   "id": "R026",
   "name": "Preview Pending Transfers",
   "description": "Before applying a transfer, the system must show a preview of the proposed changes, including the number of items and their source and destination locations, and require confirmation before making the changes.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D04"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "A preview and confirmation reduce accidental transfer changes, but they support rather than enable the system's broader workflows."
  },
  {
   "id": "R027",
   "tag": "[granularity settled]",
   "name": "Query and Select Transfer Candidates",
   "description": "The system must allow authorized staff to query candidate materials for transfer or other administrative processing using conditions such as material type, section, genre, or circulation history, and to manually select individual titles or items, including only part of a larger candidate set, for subsequent processing.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D04",
    "D15",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "D04, D15, and D20 request selecting transfer candidates, which makes transfer workflows more targeted but is not needed for reporting or other core functions."
  },
  {
   "id": "R028",
   "name": "Restrict Transfer Permissions",
   "description": "The system must restrict item transfers to authorized roles, including managers, administrators, or transfer coordinators, and prevent unauthorized staff from performing transfers.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D04"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Role restrictions reduce the risk of unauthorized transfers, although this control applies to a narrower workflow than the system's general access management."
  },
  {
   "id": "R029",
   "name": "Revert Transferred Items",
   "description": "The system must automatically or manually return transferred Items to their original Branches after a configured period or when configured criteria are met, including time-based conditions and Item-status or destination events.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D04",
    "D10",
    "D15",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "D04, D10, D15, and D20 request reversion to manage temporary transfers, but transfers can still be handled without automatic or criteria-based returns."
  },
  {
   "id": "R030",
   "name": "Save Reusable Queries",
   "description": "The system must allow users to save queries for repeated use, including recurring transfer and reporting tasks.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D04",
    "D15",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Reusable queries reduce repeated setup for recurring tasks, although users can still run those tasks by recreating queries."
  },
  {
   "id": "R031",
   "name": "Transfer History Records",
   "description": "The system must retain transfer activity for audit and expose item transfer history so staff can review completed and reverted transfers and determine how often an item has moved.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D04"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Transfer history helps staff audit movements and answer item-history questions, but it is specific to the transfer utility."
  },
  {
   "id": "R032",
   "tag": "[granularity settled]",
   "name": "Transfer Item Batches",
   "description": "The system must provide authorized staff with a utility to transfer batches of selected Items between Branches or other locations, including mobile libraries, outreach collections, warehouses, book sales, and event locations, and to update the selected Items’ location records to the transfer destination.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D04",
    "D15",
    "D20",
    "D10"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Staff need batch transfers to update item locations across the varied branches and other locations described in the sources, though other reporting and library operations can function without this utility."
  },
  {
   "id": "R033",
   "name": "Delayed Transit Items Report",
   "description": "The system must generate one report of items that have remained in transit longer than a configurable number of days, with views per branch and system-wide. The report must combine transit-to and transit-from items, identify items with no arrival date and an overdue departure date, and allow sorting by due date. Seven days is suggested as the default threshold.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D05",
    "D10",
    "D15",
    "D18"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "The report helps staff investigate overdue transit items, while the broader system can operate without this particular exception report."
  },
  {
   "id": "R034",
   "name": "Missing Damaged Items Report",
   "description": "The system must provide a report of missing and damaged items by branch. The report must include item condition notes and support date ranges for trend analysis.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D05",
    "D10",
    "D15",
    "D18"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Branch-level missing and damaged-item trends inform collection oversight, but this specialized report is not needed for other reporting workflows."
  },
  {
   "id": "R035",
   "name": "Audit Record Deletions",
   "description": "The system must retain an audit record of successful deletions, including record type, record identifier, timestamp, user, and user location. This tracking must cover purge activity and other record deletions.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D06",
    "D07",
    "D10",
    "D15"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Deletion audit records help administrators investigate changes across several source documents, but the system's reporting workflows can run without the audit feature."
  },
  {
   "id": "R036",
   "tag": "[granularity settled]",
   "name": "Batch Item Status Conversion",
   "description": "The system must support converting multiple Items from one status to another in a batch, such as changing Items from missing to discard or weed.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D06",
    "D10",
    "D15"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "The three source documents support batch status changes as a useful collection-management workflow, while staff can still change item statuses individually without it."
  },
  {
   "id": "R037",
   "name": "Confirm Purge Deletions",
   "description": "The system must require a separate confirmation step before executing purge deletions, distinct from identifying and reviewing candidates.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D06"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "A separate confirmation step helps prevent accidental purge deletions, but it supports rather than enables candidate identification and review."
  },
  {
   "id": "R038",
   "name": "Delete Itemless Records",
   "description": "The system must provide a method to delete records that have no items attached during collection cleanup.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D06",
    "D10",
    "D15"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Removing itemless records helps keep the catalog clean, although users can operate the reporting system without this cleanup method."
  },
  {
   "id": "R039",
   "name": "Delete Volumes With Copies",
   "description": "The system must provide a method to delete volume entries together with their associated copy entries during collection cleanup.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D06",
    "D10",
    "D15"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Deleting volumes with associated copies supports collection cleanup, but it is a specialized maintenance operation rather than a general reporting dependency."
  },
  {
   "id": "R040",
   "tag": "[granularity settled]",
   "name": "Deleted Last-Copy Reports",
   "description": "The system must provide reports identifying deleted Items that were previously the last copy in a library system or facility, supporting catalogers' WorldCat updates.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D06",
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D15"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Catalogers can use this report to update WorldCat when a former last copy is deleted, but the system can operate without this specialized historical report."
  },
  {
   "id": "R041",
   "name": "Identify Purge Candidates",
   "description": "The system must identify item records eligible for purging using customizable, combinable criteria, including status (such as missing, discard/weed, or damaged), time spent in a status, and time since last circulation.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D06",
    "D10",
    "D15"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Customizable purge criteria help staff identify records for collection cleanup, but review and deletion workflows can be delivered separately."
  },
  {
   "id": "R042",
   "tag": "[granularity settled]",
   "name": "Status Conversion Assistance",
   "description": "The system must provide a report or workflow to assist with converting multiple Items from one status to another.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D06",
    "D10",
    "D15"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Requested in three source documents, this workflow would help staff identify items for status conversion, while the conversion task itself can be handled through other means."
  },
  {
   "id": "R043",
   "tag": "[granularity settled]",
   "name": "Filter Patron Reports",
   "description": "The system must allow patron queries and reports to be limited by age ranges calculated from Patrons' birth dates, ZIP code, county of residence, home Branch, patron type, and preferred language. Users must be able to configure the age brackets used for filtering, including user-defined brackets such as 0–5, 6–10, and 11–15, and combine these filters with other conditions using AND and OR logic.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D08",
    "D10"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "D08 and D10 request configurable patron filters that support program planning, while the source’s emphasis on importance does not make this capability necessary for system operation."
  },
  {
   "id": "R044",
   "tag": "[granularity settled]",
   "name": "Group Patron Reports",
   "description": "The system must group patron queries and reports by age ranges calculated from Patrons' birth dates, ZIP code, county of residence, home Branch, patron type, and preferred language, using configurable age brackets such as 0–5, 6–10, and 11–15, and show aggregates such as circulation counts and patron counts for each group.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D08",
    "D10"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "D08 and D10 request demographic groupings and aggregates that support program planning, but the system can run without this specialized analysis."
  },
  {
   "id": "R045",
   "name": "Include Null Report Values",
   "description": "Report results must include records with null or blank values rather than silently excluding them, including patrons with unpopulated optional demographic fields.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D08",
    "D10",
    "D19",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Including blank values makes results more complete across several reporting contexts, although other system functions do not depend on this behavior."
  },
  {
   "id": "R046",
   "tag": "[granularity settled]",
   "name": "Export Inactive Patron Results",
   "description": "The system must allow users to export inactive patron report results to CSV.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D09",
    "D10"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "CSV export makes inactive-patron results easier to analyze and share, but the report remains usable without this additional output option."
  },
  {
   "id": "R047",
   "tag": "[granularity settled]",
   "name": "Generate Inactive Patron Reports",
   "description": "The system must generate lists of patrons with no circulation or electronic activity during a configurable number of days. Electronic activity includes account or OPAC logins, online holds, online renewals, and logged access to integrated digital collections. Users must be able to select System, Home Library, County, or another required organizational level, include current mailing addresses, separately identify patrons with outstanding fines, and exclude specified categories such as do-not-disturb, VIP, staff, or opted-out patrons.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D09",
    "D10"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "These reports help libraries review inactive accounts and outstanding fines at useful organizational levels, although they are a specialized management task."
  },
  {
   "id": "R048",
   "tag": "[granularity settled]",
   "name": "Process Reports in Background",
   "description": "The system must support background processing of inactive patron reports and retrieval of completed results.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D09",
    "D10"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Background processing helps staff retrieve results without waiting on a long-running inactive-patron report, though this report-specific convenience builds on broader processing capabilities."
  },
  {
   "id": "R049",
   "tag": "[granularity settled]",
   "name": "Add Authorized Canned Reports",
   "description": "Authorized users must be able to add canned reports according to their permissions.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Adding authorized canned reports lets staff tailor the report catalog to their work, while the existing reports and templates can still support reporting without this capability."
  },
  {
   "id": "R050",
   "name": "Anonymized Demographic Statistics",
   "description": "The system must produce demographic statistics, including transactions by geographic region and age range, using anonymized data that does not identify individual patrons.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D17",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Anonymized demographic statistics support planning while protecting patron identity, but they are one analytical use of the reporting system."
  },
  {
   "id": "R051",
   "tag": "[granularity settled]",
   "name": "Associate Financial Records",
   "description": "The system must associate fines, charges, waivers, and ecommerce transactions with Patron and Item records.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D11"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Linking financial records with patron and item records supports useful account and collection analysis, although general reporting can proceed without every such association."
  },
  {
   "id": "R052",
   "tag": "[granularity settled]",
   "name": "Bibliographic Record Reports",
   "description": "The system must provide periodic management reports identifying bibliographic records with holds and bibliographic records without item records.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "D10 requests periodic checks for records with holds or without items, helping catalogers identify records that may need attention."
  },
  {
   "id": "R053",
   "name": "Cancel Report Execution",
   "description": "Users must be able to cancel a report that is scheduled or currently running.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D19",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Cancellation helps users recover from unwanted or resource-intensive report runs, but it is a control around execution rather than a reporting prerequisite."

You read one input document against the current requirements list. The user message is JSON with the document (id, path, full text) and the FULL list of current requirements, numbered by index (index, name, description).

Return two lists:

1. supports: the indices of every requirement this document states or clearly implies, per the definition below. Topic overlap is not support: the document must ask for, or describe as needed, what the requirement says the system must do or be; supporting a part of a requirement counts. Use only indices from the list; an empty list is fine.

2. missed: requirements stated or clearly implied in this document that no listed requirement covers, even in other words or at a different level of detail. An empty list is the expected answer when the list is complete. A detail of a listed capability is not missed; ignore it. Options, fields, filters, sort orders, display rules, thresholds and similar details of one capability belong inside that capability's description, never in a separate requirement. Several distinct capabilities are never one requirement, even when they come from the same document, thread or stakeholder; sharing a topic is not a reason to merge. Only explicit asks or clearly implied needs count. An open question, a complaint without a request, an aside, or a remark about what people do is not a requirement, and you add no capability the source does not mention (for example no extra operators or options for a query tool). Skip small talk and project process (meeting schedules, who should be interviewed, testing and QA process, assumptions about the team). Documentation and training that a source states as requirements of the software or product (for example user documentation items in a draft specification) are requirements and are kept. Each requirement has a short descriptive name (3 to 8 words) and a one-paragraph description that keeps the concrete facts (numbers, fields, roles). The description states only what the system must do or be: no provenance (which document, who said it) and no priority prose. Source priority signals go in source_priority_note instead: when a source marks the item with an explicit priority marker (for example [*] or "High") or calls it critical, mandatory, legally required or non-negotiable, write a short note naming the document id (for example "D10 marks this High; D06 calls it critical"); otherwise null. A note describes only its own item: never attach a signal a source gives for a different capability.

Definition of a requirement: A requirement describes one capability, rule or quality the system must provide, at the level a tester would write one acceptance test for. It names what, for whom, and under what condition, and it is independent of how it is implemented. Two statements are the same requirement if a tester would write one test for both. A statement is too broad if its acceptance test would have to be several unrelated tests. A statement is too narrow if it only makes sense as a detail of another requirement, such as one filter option of a report.

Example of a statement that is too broad: "Staff can manage item transfers between branches, including selecting candidate items by circulation history and keeping an audit history of every completed transfer." This is exactly two requirements: (1) select transfer candidates by circulation history, (2) record an audit history of completed transfers.
Example of statements that are too narrow: "The inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch" and "The inactive patron report can be filtered by patron profile". These are one requirement: the inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch and patron profile.

messages.content:
You read one input document against the current requirements list. The user message is JSON with the document (id, path, full text) and the FULL list of current requirements, numbered by index (index, name, description).

Return two lists:

1. supports: the indices of every requirement this document states or clearly implies, per the definition below. Topic overlap is not support: the document must ask for, or describe as needed, what the requirement says the system must do or be; supporting a part of a requirement counts. Use only indices from the list; an empty list is fine.

2. missed: requirements stated or clearly implied in this document that no listed requirement covers, even in other words or at a different level of detail. An empty list is the expected answer when the list is complete. A detail of a listed capability is not missed; ignore it. Options, fields, filters, sort orders, display rules, thresholds and similar details of one capability belong inside that capability's description, never in a separate requirement. Several distinct capabilities are never one requirement, even when they come from the same document, thread or stakeholder; sharing a topic is not a reason to merge. Only explicit asks or clearly implied needs count. An open question, a complaint without a request, an aside, or a remark about what people do is not a requirement, and you add no capability the source does not mention (for example no extra operators or options for a query tool). Skip small talk and project process (meeting schedules, who should be interviewed, testing and QA process, assumptions about the team). Documentation and training that a source states as requirements of the software or product (for example user documentation items in a draft specification) are requirements and are kept. Each requirement has a short descriptive name (3 to 8 words) and a one-paragraph description that keeps the concrete facts (numbers, fields, roles). The description states only what the system must do or be: no provenance (which document, who said it) and no priority prose. Source priority signals go in source_priority_note instead: when a source marks the item with an explicit priority marker (for example [*] or "High") or calls it critical, mandatory, legally required or non-negotiable, write a short note naming the document id (for example "D10 marks this High; D06 calls it critical"); otherwise null. A note describes only its own item: never attach a signal a source gives for a different capability.

Definition of a requirement: A requirement describes one capability, rule or quality the system must provide, at the level a tester would write one acceptance test for. It names what, for whom, and under what condition, and it is independent of how it is implemented. Two statements are the same requirement if a tester would write one test for both. A statement is too broad if its acceptance test would have to be several unrelated tests. A statement is too narrow if it only makes sense as a detail of another requirement, such as one filter option of a report.

Example of a statement that is too broad: "Staff can manage item transfers between branches, including selecting candidate items by circulation history and keeping an audit history of every completed transfer." This is exactly two requirements: (1) select transfer candidates by circulation history, (2) record an audit history of completed transfers.
Example of statements that are too narrow: "The inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch" and "The inactive patron report can be filtered by patron profile". These are one requirement: the inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch and patron profile.

  "path": "meeting_tech_subcommittee_2009-06-30.txt",
  "text": "================================================================================
PINES TECHNICAL SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING NOTES
================================================================================

Date: June 30, 2009
Time: 2:00 PM - 4:30 PM EST
Location: PINES Central Office, Server Room Conference Room
Meeting Type: Technical Subcommittee - Architecture Discussion

ATTENDEES:
- Katherine Gregory (PINES Services Specialist)
- Robert Chen (Senior Systems Administrator)
- Dana Peeler (Ohoopee Regional Library) - Systems Librarian
- George Tuttle (Piedmont Regional Library) - Assistant Director
- Chris Sharp (PINES Staff Facilitator)

NOTE TAKER: Chris Sharp

1. OPENING REMARKS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Katherine opened the meeting, explaining that the technical subcommittee was
formed to discuss the architectural and implementation details of the Management
Processes reporting system. This meeting would focus on design constraints,
documentation requirements, and dependencies.

2. DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINTS - DETAILED DISCUSSION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Robert led the discussion on design constraints.

2.1 DATABASE CONSTRAINTS
Robert confirmed that the system must use a fully relational database back-end.
He noted that PostgreSQL is the current choice for PINES and it meets this
requirement. The reporting system must work WITH the relational structure,
not against it.

"I strongly recommend against denormalization for reporting," Robert said.
"Maintaining sync between a reporting warehouse and the live database creates
more problems than it solves. Modern SQL databases can handle complex analytical
queries if they're written properly."

2.2 HTML COMPLIANCE
The system must produce standards-compliant HTML. This was discussed in the
context of the web-based interface, the help system, and report output.

"We need to make sure all HTML output validates against W3C standards,"
Robert noted. "This isn't just about looks - it's about compatibility with
different browsers and assistive technologies."

2.3 DEVELOPMENT AND TRAINING ENVIRONMENT
The need for separate development, training, and production environments was
discussed.

"We have a dev server, a training server, and production," Robert explained.
"What we need is a way to migrate configurations between them. Export/import
of templates, permission settings, and saved queries."

Katherine added: "And the training environment needs to be safe - staff should
be able to experiment without risking production data."

2.4 USER RIGHTS AND ROLES
The role-based access control system was detailed:

Robert: "We need security groups and/or 'roles' that allow access control for
individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups. The system should make it
easy to change someone's permissions by simply changing their role assignment."

Key points:
- Global Admin: Full system access
- Local Admin: Branch-level reporting and configuration
- Library Manager: Run approved reports, limited template modification
- Staff: Run reports within assigned permissions
- Patron: Indirect access through OPAC displays

2.5 OPAC CONSTRAINTS
"We absolutely cannot constrain the OPAC," Robert emphasized. "The management
reporting system is separate from the public catalog. If a report is running,
it should not slow down the OPAC."

3. USER DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This section was led by Katherine.

3.1 DATA SPECIFICATIONS
The developer must provide complete data specifications for:
- Authority records
- Bibliographic records
- Order records
- Item records
- Hold/request records
- Other records maintained or accessed by Management Processes

Katherine: "Staff need to understand the data structures to write effective
queries. We need data dictionaries - field names, data types, relationships."

3.2 PROCESS DESCRIPTIONS
The developer must provide a thorough high-level description of major processes,
including:
- Bibliographic record import and export
- Validation of bibliographic records against internal and external authority
  sources
- Standard reports

3.3 ONLINE HELP SYSTEM
The system shall provide an online, hierarchical, and cross-linked help system
in HTML.

Robert: "This has to be accessible too. The help system needs to work with
screen readers."

3.4 ERROR REPORTING
The system shall provide thorough high-level error reporting and feedback,
and shall allow low-level query-specific feedback for administrators.

"When a report fails, we need to know WHY," Robert said. "Generic error messages
like 'query failed' are useless. We need specifics - which table, which field,
what kind of error."

4. ASSUMPTIONS AND DEPENDENCIES - TECHNICAL PERSPECTIVE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4.1 ENTERPRISE-LEVEL SYSTEM
AS-1: Management Processes are part of an enterprise-level Library Automation
System.

Robert: "This means we can rely on the infrastructure - redundant servers,
backup systems, network connectivity."

4.2 CENTRAL CONSOLIDATION
AS-2: Management Processes are consolidated at a central location, and accept
input and provide services to multiple locations.

"Centralization is good for reporting," Katherine noted. "We get a single
source of truth. The challenge is making sure data from all locations is complete
and current."

4.3 LIBRARY AUTOMATION DEPENDENCIES
DE-1: Management Processes rely on the data structures and functionality of
an enterprise-level Library Automation System, including Acquisitions and
Cataloging modules.

"All our data comes from the ILS," Robert said. "The reporting system doesn't
manage acquisitions or cataloging - it just reads the data."

4.4 VENDOR INTEGRATION
DE-2: Management Processes interface with a variety of vendor websites, via
published APIs and/or automated transfer of standard-format data files
(e.g., USMARC21, EDIFACT).

"We have some vendors that provide EDI ordering data," Robert explained.
"The reporting system needs to handle this data, but we can't rely on it
being present at every library."

4.5 OPAC INTEGRATION
DE-3: Management Processes interact with a patron interface (OPAC).

"Patrons create holds and circulation transactions through the OPAC," Robert
said. "The reporting system queries this data, but doesn't modify it."

5. FINE-GRAINED REPORTING REQUIREMENTS - TECHNICAL DETAILS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The technical feasibility of several fine-grained requirements was discussed:

5.1 OUTPUT FORMATS
Excel, HTML, and CSV formats are required. Robert noted that CSV is the most
reliable for data export, Excel is preferred by business users for pivot tables,
and HTML is needed for web display.

5.2 REAL-TIME vs HISTORICAL REPORTING
"Some reports need to be real-time - like 'what's overdue today,'" Robert said.
"Others are historical - 'what was the bill amount on June 30th?' We probably
need a reporting warehouse for historical data."

5.3 REPORT CANCELLATION
The ability to cancel a scheduled or running report is technically feasible,
but requires the system to check for cancellation signals during report
processing.

5.4 NULL HANDLING
"All nulls and blank fields must be included in the results," Robert noted.
"This is actually the default behavior in SQL, but we need to make sure it's
explicitly required."

5.5 SURVEY FILTERING
The ability to filter by survey name rather than survey ID requires the system
to resolve names to IDs internally.

6. ACTION ITEMS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - Robert to research reporting warehouse options for historical data
  - Katherine to compile technical requirements document
  - George to draft the architecture overview section
  - All attendees to review the fine-grained requirements for technical
    feasibility
  - Follow-up technical meeting scheduled for August 15, 2009

Meeting adjourned at 4:25 PM.

Notes prepared by: Chris Sharp
Notes distributed: July 2, 2009"

You read one input document against the current requirements list. The user message is JSON with the document (id, path, full text) and the FULL list of current requirements, numbered by index (index, name, description).

Return two lists:

1. supports: the indices of every requirement this document states or clearly implies, per the definition below. Topic overlap is not support: the document must ask for, or describe as needed, what the requirement says the system must do or be; supporting a part of a requirement counts. Use only indices from the list; an empty list is fine.

2. missed: requirements stated or clearly implied in this document that no listed requirement covers, even in other words or at a different level of detail. An empty list is the expected answer when the list is complete. A detail of a listed capability is not missed; ignore it. Options, fields, filters, sort orders, display rules, thresholds and similar details of one capability belong inside that capability's description, never in a separate requirement. Several distinct capabilities are never one requirement, even when they come from the same document, thread or stakeholder; sharing a topic is not a reason to merge. Only explicit asks or clearly implied needs count. An open question, a complaint without a request, an aside, or a remark about what people do is not a requirement, and you add no capability the source does not mention (for example no extra operators or options for a query tool). Skip small talk and project process (meeting schedules, who should be interviewed, testing and QA process, assumptions about the team). Documentation and training that a source states as requirements of the software or product (for example user documentation items in a draft specification) are requirements and are kept. Each requirement has a short descriptive name (3 to 8 words) and a one-paragraph description that keeps the concrete facts (numbers, fields, roles). The description states only what the system must do or be: no provenance (which document, who said it) and no priority prose. Source priority signals go in source_priority_note instead: when a source marks the item with an explicit priority marker (for example [*] or "High") or calls it critical, mandatory, legally required or non-negotiable, write a short note naming the document id (for example "D10 marks this High; D06 calls it critical"); otherwise null. A note describes only its own item: never attach a signal a source gives for a different capability.

Definition of a requirement: A requirement describes one capability, rule or quality the system must provide, at the level a tester would write one acceptance test for. It names what, for whom, and under what condition, and it is independent of how it is implemented. Two statements are the same requirement if a tester would write one test for both. A statement is too broad if its acceptance test would have to be several unrelated tests. A statement is too narrow if it only makes sense as a detail of another requirement, such as one filter option of a report.

Example of a statement that is too broad: "Staff can manage item transfers between branches, including selecting candidate items by circulation history and keeping an audit history of every completed transfer." This is exactly two requirements: (1) select transfer candidates by circulation history, (2) record an audit history of completed transfers.
Example of statements that are too narrow: "The inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch" and "The inactive patron report can be filtered by patron profile". These are one requirement: the inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch and patron profile.

 "document": {
  "id": "D18",
  "path": "meeting_minutes/meeting_2009-07-20_minutes.txt",
  "text": "================================================================================
PINES REPORTS WORKING GROUP - SECOND MEETING MINUTES
================================================================================

Date: July 20, 2009
Time: 9:30 AM - 12:00 PM EST
Location: Georgia Public Library Service, Conference Room A, Atlanta, GA
Meeting Type: Regular Working Group Meeting

ATTENDEES:
- Katherine Gregory (PINES Services Specialist) - Chair
- LaToya Davidson (Twin Lakes Library System) - Library Director
- Jennifer Durham (Statesboro Regional Library System) - Assistant Library Director
- Dana Peeler (Ohoopee Regional Library) - Systems Librarian
- Susan Sexton-Cooley (Sara Hightower Regional Library) - Assistant Library Director
- George Tuttle (Piedmont Regional Library) - Assistant Library Director
- Chris Sharp (PINES Staff Facilitator)

ABSENTEES: None

1. CALL TO ORDER AND REVIEW OF ACTION ITEMS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Katherine called the meeting to order at 9:35 AM.

Action items from the March 15 meeting:
  - Interviews with staff: COMPLETED (all members submitted reports)
  - Circulation of Galecia Group draft: COMPLETED
  - Technical subcommittee meeting: SCHEDULED for June 30 (see below)

2. INTERVIEW FINDINGS SUMMARY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Each member presented a summary of their interview findings:

LaToya Davidson (Twin Lakes): Spoke with 3 branch managers. Key themes:
  - Inventory and capacity reports are used daily
  - Financial report needs are understood at the director level
  - Need for cross-branch comparison reports

Jennifer Durham (Statesboro): Spoke with 2 branch managers and 1 director.
  Key themes:
  - Report queue visibility is important
  - Board/executive reports need to be pre-defined
  - Data quality reports are needed

Dana Peeler (Ohoopee): Spoke with 1 branch manager. Key themes:
  - Staff login needs (card swipe) - already discussed via email
  - In-transit item reports are critical for delivery coordination
  - Missing/damaged item reports are needed per branch

Susan Sexton-Cooley (Sara Hightower): Spoke with 1 branch manager. Key themes:
  - Weeding reports are frequently used
  - Shelf space utilization reports are important
  - Demographic analysis for program planning

George Tuttle (Piedmont): Spoke with 1 branch manager and 1 IT staff.
  Key themes:
  - Technical constraints (server OS, browser support)
  - User permissions and role-based access
  - Accessibility requirements

3. OPERATING ENVIRONMENT REQUIREMENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This section was led by Dana Peeler and George Tuttle, drawing on input from
their interviews.

OE-1: Management Processes must support the needs of a large, multiple-system
      library consortium. Specifically, the system must support a library
      consortium with 286 locations, 17 million annual circulations,
      purchasing and processing over 900,000 items per year. It is highly
      desirable that searches and reports can be processed during open hours
      without disrupting other system functions.

      [Discussion: George noted that Evergreen already handles this scale.
      The concern is about report processing during peak hours. We need
      background processing/queuing to prevent report generation from slowing
      down the circulation client.]

OE-2: Management Processes shall operate on a Linux or Solaris server.
      [Consensus: Both Linux and Solaris are acceptable. Most PINES
      installations use Linux, but some larger systems use Solaris.]

OE-3: Management Processes shall be accessible through a web-browser or a
      Windows-compatible client.
      [Discussion: This is critical - some libraries prefer browser-based
      access (no client install), others prefer the dedicated client for
      better performance.]

OE-4: If web-browser based, Management Processes shall be accessible through
      Microsoft Internet Explorer (v.6.0 and later) and Mozilla Firefox
      (v.2.0 and later).
      [Discussion: We need to support both IE and Firefox because different
      libraries standardize on different browsers. IE 6 is still common in
      our library environments, even though it's old.]

OE-5: Management Processes shall be accessible with screen-reading software,
      screen-magnification software, and other software programs designed to
      increase accessibility.
      [Discussion: Susan emphasized this is a legal requirement for public
      institutions. We need to support JAWS, NVDA, ZoomText, and other
      assistive technologies. Section 508 compliance is mandatory.]

4. DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This section was led by George Tuttle, drawing on his IT interview.

CO-1: Management Processes shall use a fully relational database back-end.
      [Discussion: Evergreen already uses PostgreSQL. We need to ensure our
      reporting layer works properly with the relational structure.]

CO-2: Management Processes shall produce standards-compliant HTML.
      [Discussion: All web output needs to be valid HTML. This affects report
      display, help system, and any web-based UI components.]

CO-3: Management Processes shall provide a development and training environment
      with the ability to migrate configurations to a production environment.
      [Discussion: Katherine noted that Evergreen development follows this
      pattern - developers have separate environments. We need to make sure
      report templates and configurations can be exported/imported.]

CO-4: User rights and privileges will be controlled through security groups
      and/or "roles" that allow access control for individuals, workgroups,
      and arbitrary staff groups.
      [Discussion: George confirmed this is essential. We need flexible
      role-based access control.]

CO-5: These requirements shall not constrain functionality or features of the
      Online Public Access Catalog (OPAC) module.
      [Discussion: The management processes are separate from the public-
      facing catalog. Changes to management reporting should not affect
      patron access.]

5. USER DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Katherine led a discussion on user documentation needs:

UD-1: The software developer shall provide complete data specifications for
      authority records, bibliographic records, order records, item records,
      hold/request records, and other records maintained or accessed by
      Management Processes.

      [Discussion: Staff need to understand the data structures to write
      effective queries. Data dictionaries are essential.]

UD-2: The software developer shall provide a thorough high-level description
      of major processes, including bibliographic record import and export,
      validation of bibliographic records against internal and external
      authority sources, and standard reports.

      [Discussion: Process flow documentation helps staff understand how
      data moves through the system.]

UD-3: The system shall provide an online, hierarchical, and cross-linked help
      system in HTML that describes and illustrates all system functions.

      [Discussion: Context-sensitive help is critical. Staff shouldn't have
      to leave the system to find documentation.]

UD-4: The system shall provide thorough high-level error reporting and feedback
      and shall allow low-level query-specific feedback for Local and Global
      System Administrators from the front-end interface.

      [Discussion: When reports fail, staff need to understand why. Error
      messages should be meaningful.]

6. ASSUMPTIONS AND DEPENDENCIES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
AS-1: Management Processes are part of an enterprise-level Library Automation
      System.
      [Discussion: This means we can rely on the infrastructure being
      enterprise-grade. Evergreen is that system for PINES.]

AS-2: Management Processes are consolidated at a central location, and accept
      input and provide services to multiple locations.
      [Discussion: Centralization enables consistent reporting but requires
      good network connectivity.]

DE-1: Management Processes rely on the data structures and functionality of an
      enterprise-level Library Automation System, including Acquisitions and
      Cataloging modules.
      [Discussion: The data we report on comes from the ILS. We don't manage
      acquisitions or cataloging ourselves.]

DE-2: Management Processes interface with a variety of vendor websites, via
      published APIs and/or automated transfer of standard-format data files
      (e.g., USMARC21, EDIFACT).
      [Discussion: Some libraries use external vendors for certain functions.
      Our reporting needs to handle data from these sources too.]

DE-3: Management Processes interact with a patron interface, also known as an
      Online Public Access Catalog (OPAC).
      [Discussion: Patron data (holds, circulation) is created in the OPAC.
      Our reports need to query this data.]

7. REPORTS WORKING GROUP MISSION REVIEW
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Katherine reviewed the working group's mission:

  Reports Working Group Mission:
  1. Document optimal Reports functionality within a future Evergreen release
     and develop a list of requirements.
  2. Become the Reports testing group, through which all new Reports development
     would be filtered.
  3. Compile a list of reports needed for an Executive Reports Interface.
  4. Determine and create templates needed for all PINES libraries.

All members agreed the mission is still accurate and relevant.

8. ACTION ITEMS AND NEXT STEPS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - Technical subcommittee meeting: June 30, 2009 (Katherine to send agenda)
  - Complete draft of requirements document: by September 1, 2009
  - Katherine to circulate consolidated requirements list
  - George and Dana to draft technical architecture section
  - All members to continue gathering detailed report requirements

Meeting adjourned at 12:00 PM.

Minutes prepared by: Katherine Gregory, PINES Services Specialist
Minutes distributed: July 22, 2009"

  {

Return two lists:

1. supports: the indices of every requirement this document states or clearly implies, per the definition below. Topic overlap is not support: the document must ask for, or describe as needed, what the requirement says the system must do or be; supporting a part of a requirement counts. Use only indices from the list; an empty list is fine.

2. missed: requirements stated or clearly implied in this document that no listed requirement covers, even in other words or at a different level of detail. An empty list is the expected answer when the list is complete. A detail of a listed capability is not missed; ignore it. Options, fields, filters, sort orders, display rules, thresholds and similar details of one capability belong inside that capability's description, never in a separate requirement. Several distinct capabilities are never one requirement, even when they come from the same document, thread or stakeholder; sharing a topic is not a reason to merge. Only explicit asks or clearly implied needs count. An open question, a complaint without a request, an aside, or a remark about what people do is not a requirement, and you add no capability the source does not mention (for example no extra operators or options for a query tool). Skip small talk and project process (meeting schedules, who should be interviewed, testing and QA process, assumptions about the team). Documentation and training that a source states as requirements of the software or product (for example user documentation items in a draft specification) are requirements and are kept. Each requirement has a short descriptive name (3 to 8 words) and a one-paragraph description that keeps the concrete facts (numbers, fields, roles). The description states only what the system must do or be: no provenance (which document, who said it) and no priority prose. Source priority signals go in source_priority_note instead: when a source marks the item with an explicit priority marker (for example [*] or "High") or calls it critical, mandatory, legally required or non-negotiable, write a short note naming the document id (for example "D10 marks this High; D06 calls it critical"); otherwise null. A note describes only its own item: never attach a signal a source gives for a different capability.

Definition of a requirement: A requirement describes one capability, rule or quality the system must provide, at the level a tester would write one acceptance test for. It names what, for whom, and under what condition, and it is independent of how it is implemented. Two statements are the same requirement if a tester would write one test for both. A statement is too broad if its acceptance test would have to be several unrelated tests. A statement is too narrow if it only makes sense as a detail of another requirement, such as one filter option of a report.

Example of a statement that is too broad: "Staff can manage item transfers between branches, including selecting candidate items by circulation history and keeping an audit history of every completed transfer." This is exactly two requirements: (1) select transfer candidates by circulation history, (2) record an audit history of completed transfers.
Example of statements that are too narrow: "The inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch" and "The inactive patron report can be filtered by patron profile". These are one requirement: the inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch and patron profile.
